definition_zh: 推迟；延期；暂缓；把……置于次要地位；使延缓发生
definition_en: to move an event or decision to a later time, to keep something from happening yet, or to place one thing after another in order or importance
core_image: 行李箱上的日期签被撕下，重新贴上一张更晚的日子
scene: 赛前一夜下起大雨，球场边的排水沟满得往外溢，裁判举着喇叭跟两队教练商量。The referee decided to postpone the match until the following weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 postpone 指「把比赛改到更晚的时间」（第 1 个义项：活动延期举行）；句意为裁判决定把比赛推迟到下个周末。图中可辨识场景：积水的球场、举着喇叭的裁判、围在边线旁的两队教练。

pos.zh: 推迟；延期；暂缓；使居次位

derivatives.zh: 由 postpone 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「延期；推迟」
由 postpone 加 -ed 构成的过去分词作定语，义为「被推迟的」

senses.title: To move an event to a later time
senses.definition: to arrange for an event, appointment or journey to take place later than was planned
senses.definitionCN: 把活动、约会或行程安排在比原计划更晚的时间
senses.example: They postponed the wedding until the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把婚礼推迟到春天举行。
senses.why: The Latin verb postponere is built from post, after, and ponere, to place, so the event is literally put further back on the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 postponere 由 post（在后）与 ponere（放置）组成，事情就是被「放到日历更靠后的位置」上，所以是改期。

senses.title: To leave a decision or action for later
senses.definition: to delay dealing with a decision or action without abandoning it
senses.definitionCN: 暂不处理某个决定或行动，但并没有放弃它
senses.example: The committee postponed its verdict on the disputed plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会暂缓就那份有争议的方案作出裁决。
senses.why: Ponere only says where a thing is put, so the verb can put a decision aside just as easily as it puts a date back, and either way the matter stays open.
senses.whyCN: ponere 只交代「把东西放在哪儿」，所以这个动词能把决定搁到一边，也能把日期往后挪，两种做法都让事情悬着。

senses.title: To place something after another in rank
senses.definition: to treat one thing as less urgent or less important than another and let it come second
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事的紧迫性或重要性低于另一事，让它排在后面
senses.example: He postponed his own career so that his brother could study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己事业的事往后放，好让弟弟出国读书。
senses.why: The spatial picture turns abstract: priority is also a line with things placed along it, and whatever is put behind has to wait its turn.
senses.whyCN: 这个空间画面转向抽象：优先次序同样是一条排队线，被放到后面的东西就得等轮到自己。

senses.title: To slow a process so that it happens later
senses.definition: to hold back a natural or gradual process so that its results appear at a later stage
senses.definitionCN: 使自然的或渐进的过程放慢，让结果出现得更晚
senses.example: Early treatment can postpone the worst effects of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 早期治疗可以延缓这种疾病最严重的影响。
senses.why: If a single event can be placed later on a calendar, a process with an expected end can be pushed back in the same way, and that is how the verb reaches illness and ageing.
senses.whyCN: 既然一件事能在日程上往后放，一个有预期终点的过程也能照样往后推，动词于是走进了疾病与衰老这类话题。

intro.en: Postpone is Latin postponere carried into English almost whole: post meant after and ponere meant to place, so the word has always been about putting something further back.
intro.cn: postpone 几乎原样搬自拉丁语 postponere：post 意为「在后」，ponere 意为「放置」，所以这个词从头到尾说的都是把东西往后放。

items.en: Ponere meant to put, set or place, and it built a large family of English words about position and arrangement.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、安放，它造出了一大批表示位置与排列的英语词。

items.en: The prefix post meant after or behind, whether the distance was measured in space or in time.
items.cn: 前缀 post 意为「在后」，既可量空间，也可量时间。

items.en: Postponere joined the two: to put one thing after another, and in later usage to put an affair off to a later date.
items.cn: postponere 把两者合起来：把一物放到另一物之后，后来也指把事情挪到更晚的日子。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century, first for placing things in order, then for shifting dates and plans.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，先用于按次序摆放，随后用于改动日期与计划。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly for dates, decisions and processes, while the older ranking sense survives in formal writing.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用它谈日期、决定与过程，较早的「排序」义则留在正式书面语里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin verb ponere; the near-meaning group collects verbs for moving something to a later time.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁动词 ponere 构成的词；近义组收表示把事情挪到更晚时间的动词。

entries.definition: The act of moving an event or decision to a later time.
entries.definitionCN: 把活动或决定改到更晚时间的做法；延期。

entries.definition: One of the parts that a larger whole is put together from.
entries.definitionCN: 组成整体的部件之一；成分。

entries.definition: A person who is placed against another in a contest.
entries.definitionCN: 在竞赛中被放到对手位置上的人；对手。

entries.definition: The place where someone or something has been put.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物被放置的地方；位置。

entries.definition: To make something happen later than planned.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事比计划更晚发生；延迟。

entries.definition: To put off an action until a later time, often officially.
entries.definitionCN: 把行动正式推迟到以后。

entries.definition: To change an arranged time to a later one.
entries.definitionCN: 把约定的时间往后改；推迟。

entries.definition: To decide not to continue with a plan for now.
entries.definitionCN: 决定暂时不推进某项计划；搁置。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of placing, and every sense is a different place on a line: a calendar, a queue of priorities, a process running late.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语里表示「放置」的动词，每个义项都是同一条线上的不同位置：日历、优先次序的队列、走慢了的过程。

normal.en: Post- means after and ponere means place, so postpone is simply to place after.
normal.cn: post- 意为「在后」，ponere 意为「放置」，postpone 就是「放到后面」。

normal.en: The family shares ponere: component is put together, opponent is put against you, position is where a thing is put.
normal.cn: 这一族词共用 ponere：component 是被拼在一起，opponent 是被放到你对面，position 是被放置的地方。

normal.en: A postponed match has a new date; a postponed decision has no date at all, only a later one.
normal.cn: postponed 的比赛有新日期；被搁置的决定根本没有日期，只有「以后」。

normal.en: The noun is postponement, and it takes -ment like movement and agreement.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 postponement，和 movement、agreement 一样加 -ment。

normal.en: Formal writing still says that one aim is postponed to another, meaning placed below it.
normal.cn: 正式书面语里还会说某个目标被 postponed to 另一个目标，意思是排在它之下。

abstract.en: To postpone is to move a thing down a line without taking it off the line.
abstract.cn: 推迟是把一样东西在队伍里往后挪，而不是把它从队伍里拿掉。

abstract.en: A calendar is a row of places, and the word treats time as something you can rearrange.
abstract.cn: 日历是一排位置，这个词把时间当成可以重新摆放的东西。

abstract.en: What is put behind still exists; that is why postponement is not cancellation.
abstract.cn: 被放到后面的东西依然存在，所以延期并不等于取消。

examples.en: They postponed the wedding until the spring.
examples.cn: 他们把婚礼推迟到春天举行。

examples.en: The judge postponed the hearing for two weeks.
examples.cn: 法官把听证会推迟了两周。

examples.en: Nothing was cancelled; every item on the list was simply postponed.
examples.cn: 什么都没取消，清单上每一项只是被往后推了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕事拖」——越怕事情办不成，越往后拖；postpone 就是推迟、延期。

root: 拉丁语 post-（在后）+ ponere（放置）→ postponere（放到后面）→ 英语 postpone；同族有 component、opponent、position。

sensesIntro.en: One image of placing runs through the senses: a date moved back, a decision left pending, a task pushed down the queue, a process slowed.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项贯穿着同一个「放置」的画面：日期后移、决定悬着、任务排到后面、过程放慢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a date on a luggage tag scraped off and written again, later than before.
core.cn: 核心意象：行李牌上的日期被刮掉，重新写上一个更晚的日子。

branches.en: a stadium filling with rain while the referee talks to both coaches
branches.cn: 球场积起雨水，裁判与两位教练商量

branches.en: a verdict left unsigned on the committee table
branches.cn: 委员会桌上那份没有签字的裁决

branches.en: one career set down so another can go forward
branches.cn: 一份事业被放下，好让另一份往前走

branches.en: a doctor describing how treatment buys time
branches.cn: 医生说明治疗如何争取时间

branches.en: a date and a disease both pushed back
branches.cn: 一个日期与一种病都被往后推

intro.en: A Latin prefix of delay and a Latin verb of placing carry the word; English then adds -ment for the act and -ed for the result.
intro.cn: 一个表示「在后」的拉丁前缀和一个表示「放置」的拉丁动词撑起这个词，英语再用 -ment 表示行为、用 -ed 表示结果。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

scene: 灶上的汤滚了，白汽把窗玻璃蒙住，母亲用抹布垫着手去掀锅盖。She lifted the lid of the pot and the smell of ginger filled the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 pot 指「锅」（第 1 个义项：做饭用的深圆容器）；句意为她掀开锅盖，姜的香味立刻充满厨房。图中可辨识场景：跳动着的锅盖、蒙住玻璃的白汽、垫着抹布的手。

pos.zh: 锅；罐；壶；一锅之量；花盆；赌注总额

collocations.phrase: the pot calling the kettle black

derivatives.zh: 由 pot 加表示工艺与场所的 -ery 构成，义为「陶器；陶艺作坊」
由 pot 加表示做某事者的 -er 构成，义为「陶工」
由 pot 加 -ed 构成的过去分词作定语，义为「盆栽的；罐装的」
由 pot 加表示「一……之量」的 -ful 构成，义为「一锅（罐）之量」

senses.title: A deep round container for cooking or storing
senses.definition: a deep round vessel, usually with a lid, used for cooking food or keeping things in
senses.definitionCN: 通常带盖的深圆容器，用来做饭或存放东西
senses.example: She left the soup simmering in a heavy iron pot.
senses.exampleCN: 她把汤留在一口厚重的铁锅里慢慢炖着。
senses.why: Old English pott named a rounded vessel before it named any particular use, so cooking is only one of the jobs the container was given.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pott 先指一种圆鼓鼓的容器，并不限定用途，做饭只是人们后来交给它的活儿之一。

senses.title: The amount a pot holds
senses.definition: as much as a pot contains, used as a rough measure in cooking and serving
senses.definitionCN: 一锅或一罐所装的分量，在烹饪与待客时用作粗略的计量
senses.example: He made a pot of coffee for the four of them.
senses.exampleCN: 他煮了一壶咖啡给四个人喝。
senses.why: A container word slides to its contents because the two are always seen together, and English lets pot measure coffee or soup without any extra suffix.
senses.whyCN: 容器和里面的东西总是一起出现，于是容器词顺势指内容物；英语不必加后缀，pot 就能直接量咖啡或汤。

senses.title: A container for a growing plant
senses.definition: a round container filled with soil in which a plant is grown indoors or on a windowsill
senses.definitionCN: 装满泥土、在室内或窗台上种花的圆形容器
senses.example: The basil on the windowsill needs a bigger pot.
senses.exampleCN: 窗台上的罗勒需要换一个更大的花盆。
senses.why: When clay vessels were stood in gardens and on windowsills, the same word that named a kitchen vessel came to name the vessel a plant lives in.
senses.whyCN: 当陶制容器被摆到院子里和窗台上，原本指厨房器皿的词就转而指植物所住的容器。

senses.title: To plant something in a pot
senses.definition: to put a plant into a container filled with soil so that it can grow there
senses.definitionCN: 把植物放进装了土的容器里，让它在其中生长
senses.example: She potted the young tomato plants before the first frost.
senses.exampleCN: 初霜之前，她把番茄苗移栽进了盆里。
senses.why: English turns nouns into verbs without adding anything, so the name of the container became the name of the act of putting a plant into it.
senses.whyCN: 英语可以不添任何成分就把名词用作动词，于是容器的名字变成了「把植物放进容器」这个动作的名字。

senses.title: The money staked in a card game
senses.definition: the total amount of money that players have put into the middle of the table in a game of cards
senses.definitionCN: 牌局中玩家押到桌面中央的钱的总数
senses.example: By the last hand there was a small fortune in the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 到最后一局时，桌上的赌注已经是一笔不小的钱。
senses.why: Card players drop their stakes into a central dish, and English simply moved the name of that dish onto the money it held, keeping the picture of a shared vessel.
senses.whyCN: 牌手把赌注丢进桌子中央的盘子里，英语直接把盘子的名字挪到里面的钱上，共用一只容器的画面留了下来。

intro.en: Pot is an old Germanic vessel word. Whether it was lent to Latin or borrowed from Latin is still argued, so the deeper origin is usually given with a hedge.
intro.cn: pot 是一个古老的日耳曼语容器词。它究竟是借给了拉丁语，还是从拉丁语借来，至今仍有争论，所以更远的来历通常要加一句「一般认为」。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic word for a rounded vessel; the asterisk marks a form rebuilt by comparing later languages, not one found written down.
items.cn: 这是为「圆形容器」重构出来的日耳曼语词；星号表示它是靠比较后世语言推出来的，并非有文字记录的形式。

items.en: Old English pott names a deep vessel, and this is the form English has kept to the present day.
items.cn: 古英语 pott 指深腹容器，英语一直把这个形式保留到今天。

items.en: Many dictionaries think the Germanic word was borrowed from a Vulgar Latin pottus for a drinking vessel, but the direction of the borrowing is not settled.
items.cn: 不少词典认为这个日耳曼词借自俗拉丁语 pottus（饮器），但借用的方向至今没有定论。

items.en: If the vessel word does go back to Latin, its ultimate root is potare, to drink, with potio, a drink, beside it.
items.cn: 如果这个容器词确实可追溯到拉丁语，它更远的根就是 potare（饮），旁边的 potio 意为饮料。

items.en: Modern English extended the vessel to flower pots, to the stakes in a card game, and to the verb of planting.
items.cn: 现代英语把这件容器扩展到花盆、牌桌上的赌注，还把它用作「栽种」的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the vessel itself; the near-meaning group gathers other kitchen and table containers.
note.cn: 形近组收直接由这件容器构成的词；近义组收厨房与餐桌上其他容器词。

entries.definition: Pots and other objects made of baked clay.
entries.definitionCN: 陶土烧成的锅、罐等器物；陶器。

entries.definition: A person who makes pots and other clay vessels.
entries.definitionCN: 制作陶罐等器皿的人；陶工。

entries.definition: As much as a single pot will hold.
entries.definitionCN: 一锅或一罐的分量。

entries.definition: A thick soup or stew cooked in a pot.
entries.definitionCN: 在锅里熬成的浓汤；菜糊。

entries.definition: A shallow metal container used for cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 较浅的金属锅；平底锅。

entries.definition: A container with a spout and handle, used for boiling water.
entries.definitionCN: 带壶嘴和把手、用来烧水的壶。

entries.definition: A wide-mouthed container of glass or clay, used for storing food.
entries.definitionCN: 广口的玻璃或陶制容器，用来存放食物；罐子。

entries.definition: A very large pot used for boiling over a fire.
entries.definitionCN: 在火上煮东西用的大锅。

normalIntro.en: The word has named a round vessel for over a thousand years, and most of its other uses are that vessel seen from a different angle.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指一种圆容器已有一千多年，它其余的用法大多只是从不同角度去看这件容器。

normal.en: Old English pott already meant a deep vessel, so the word is older than any recipe written in English.
normal.cn: 古英语 pott 已经是「深容器」的意思，所以这个词比任何英语写成的菜谱都老。

normal.en: Add -ful and the vessel becomes a measure: a potful is as much as it takes to fill one.
normal.cn: 加上 -ful，容器就变成量词：potful 就是装满一只锅的分量。

normal.en: Add -er and you get the person, potter, the one who makes the vessel.
normal.cn: 加上 -er 就得到人：potter 是做这件容器的人。

normal.en: Add -ery and you get the craft and its place: pottery is both the ware and the workshop.
normal.cn: 加上 -ery 就得到手艺与场所：pottery 既指陶器，也指陶艺作坊。

normal.en: Pot luck and go to pot keep the old household picture: whatever the pot happens to hold, or a house gone to ruin.
normal.cn: pot luck 与 go to pot 都留着旧日居家的画面：锅里碰巧有什么，或者一个家败落下去。

abstract.en: A pot is defined by what it can hold, so the word slides easily from vessel to contents to the money on a table.
abstract.cn: 锅由它能装什么来定义，所以这个词很自然地从事物滑到内容，再滑到桌上的钱。

abstract.en: Round, deep and lidded: the shape is the meaning, and every new use keeps that shape somewhere in view.
abstract.cn: 圆、深、有盖：形状本身就是词义，每个新用法都在某处保留着这个形状。

abstract.en: The same word feeds a kitchen, a garden and a card table, because all three need something to put things into.
abstract.cn: 同一个词同时养活厨房、花园和牌桌，因为这三处都需要一个能装东西的容器。

examples.en: She left the soup simmering in a heavy iron pot.
examples.cn: 她把汤留在一口厚重的铁锅里慢慢炖着。

examples.en: He potted the seedlings on the balcony.
examples.cn: 他在阳台上把幼苗栽进了盆里。

examples.en: There was enough money in the pot to pay for the trip.
examples.cn: 桌上的赌注足够支付这趟旅行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡特」——汤在锅里泡得特别久；pot 就是锅、罐，也能当动词表示栽进盆里。

root: 中古英语 pott 上承古英语 pott；一般认为与俗拉丁语 pottus（饮器）有关，更远的根或为拉丁语 potare（饮），但借用方向仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a round vessel; the senses then follow what the vessel holds, where it stands, and what people do with it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一件圆容器；义项随后沿着它装什么、摆在哪里、人们拿它做什么展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick pot on a stove, its lid lifted again and again by steam.
core.cn: 核心意象：灶上一口厚底锅，锅盖被蒸汽一次次顶起。

intro.en: One old Germanic noun, pott, supplies the stem; English then builds a measure with -ful, a person with -er, a craft with -ery, and a participle with -ed.
intro.cn: 一个古老的日耳曼名词 pott 提供词干，英语再用 -ful 造量、用 -er 造人、用 -ery 造手艺、用 -ed 造分词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: possible but not yet actual; having the capacity to develop into something; (noun) the capacity to become something in the future
core_image: 一枚还没拉开的弓：力已经存着，只是尚未射出
scene: 药房里，药剂师指着说明书上的警示行。She said: Potential side effects make this drug dangerous when it is taken with alcohol.
sceneCN: 这里 potential 是「潜在的、可能发生但还没发生的」（第 1 个义项：以一种可能性的方式存在）；句意：潜在的副作用会让这种药与酒精同服时变得危险。场景要点：还没发生、但条件一凑就会发生；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Possible but not yet actual
senses.titleCN: 潜在的：可能发生，但还没发生
senses.definition: existing as a possibility rather than as a fact
senses.definitionCN: 以一种可能性的方式存在，而非作为事实存在
senses.example: The drug is potentially dangerous if taken with alcohol.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药如果与酒精同服，可能有危险。
senses.why: Latin posse means 'to be able'. Potential marks what is able to happen without having happened yet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 posse 意为“能够”。potential 标记的是“能够发生、但尚未发生”的东西。

senses.title: Having latent ability
senses.titleCN: 有潜力的：本事藏着，还没使出来
senses.definition: having an ability that is not yet developed or shown
senses.definitionCN: 拥有尚未发展或尚未显现的能力
senses.example: She is a potential national champion in the 800 metres.
senses.exampleCN: 她有可能成为 800 米全国冠军。
senses.why: The same 'able to be' applies to a person: the capacity is real, the achievement is not yet.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“能够成为”用在人身上：能力是真实的，成就还没到。

senses.title: Physics: stored energy
senses.titleCN: 势能：存着还没放出来的能量
senses.definition: energy that a body has because of its position or condition, rather than because of motion
senses.definitionCN: 物体因位置或状态而具有的能量，而非因运动而具有的能量
senses.example: The water behind the dam has a great deal of potential energy.
senses.exampleCN: 坝后的水具有大量势能。
senses.why: Energy held in place is ability waiting to be released. Physics named it with the same word for capacity.
senses.whyCN: 被位置存住的能量，就是等着被释放的“能够”。物理学用了同一个表示“能力”的词来命名它。

senses.title: Physics: electric potential
senses.titleCN: 电势：电场里某点的“位势”
senses.definition: the amount of electric potential energy per unit charge at a point in a field
senses.definitionCN: 电场中某点单位电荷所具有的电势能
senses.example: Current flows from higher to lower electric potential.
senses.exampleCN: 电流从电势较高处流向电势较低处。
senses.why: A charge at a point in a field has stored ability to move. That stored ability, measured per charge, is the potential.
senses.whyCN: 电场中某点的电荷存有移动的能力。把这份储存的能力按单位电荷计量，就是电势。

senses.title: Grammar: expressing possibility
senses.titleCN: 语法：表示可能性的语气
senses.definition: in grammar, describing a mood or form that presents something as possible rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指把某事呈现为可能而非现实的形式或语气
senses.example: In some languages the potential mood marks what may happen.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言用可能语气标记可能发生的事。
senses.why: Grammar borrows the word to name the form whose job is exactly this: stating what can be, without stating that it is.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个词，来命名那种专门做这件事的形式：说出“可能是什么”，而不说“就是什么”。

senses.title: Noun: the possibility of something
senses.titleCN: 名词：某事发生的可能性
senses.definition: the possibility that something will happen or can be developed
senses.definitionCN: 某事将会发生或可以被发展出来的可能性
senses.example: The potential for conflict remains high in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区发生冲突的可能性仍然很高。
senses.why: The adjective's abstract quality becomes a noun: not a possible thing, but possibility itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词的抽象性质变成名词：不是某个可能之物，而是“可能性”本身。

senses.title: Noun: undeveloped capacity in a person
senses.titleCN: 名词：一个人身上尚未长成的本事
senses.definition: the capacity a person has to develop and succeed in the future
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在未来发展与取得成就的能力
senses.example: The coach saw potential in the young goalkeeper.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在这个年轻守门员身上看到了潜力。
senses.why: A person is treated like a body with stored energy: what is there now is less than what it can become.
senses.whyCN: 人被当成一个储能的身体：现在已有的，少于它将来能成为的。

senses.title: Physics: potential difference
senses.titleCN: 电势差：两点之间的位势落差
senses.definition: the difference in electric potential between two points, measured in volts
senses.definitionCN: 两点之间电势的差值，以伏特计
senses.example: A battery maintains a potential difference across its terminals.
senses.exampleCN: 电池在其两端维持一个电势差。
senses.why: Difference is what makes stored ability flow. The gap between two potentials is the push that moves charge.
senses.whyCN: 落差才使储存的能力流动。两个电势之间的差距，就是推动电荷移动的那股力。

intro.en: Potential comes from the Latin verb for being able. The idea is capacity that has not yet turned into act, which is why the word serves both for people and for stored energy.
intro.cn: potential 来自拉丁语中表示“能够”的动词。其观念是“尚未变成现实的能力”，所以它既可用于人，也可用于储存的能量。

items.en: Posse meant 'to be able, to have power'. It is a compound of potis 'able' plus esse 'to be', literally 'to be able'.
items.cn: posse 意为“能够、有力量”。它由 potis“有能力的”加 esse“存在、是”构成，字面即“能够是”。

items.en: The present participle potens meant 'being able, powerful'. English potent and omnipotent come from this form.
items.cn: 现在分词 potens 意为“有能力的、强大的”。英语 potent 与 omnipotent 来自这个形式。

items.en: Potentia meant 'power, ability, capacity'. It names the quality rather than the act, which is exactly the seed of the modern word.
items.cn: potentia 意为“力量、能力、潜能”。它命名的是性质而非行动，这正是现代这个词的种子。

items.en: Potentialis was formed from potentia plus -alis, meaning 'having power or capacity'. Medieval philosophy used it for what can exist without existing yet.
items.cn: potentialis 由 potentia 加 -alis 构成，意为“具有力量或能力的”。中世纪哲学用它指“能够存在但尚未存在”的东西。

items.en: English potential enters in the 17th century, first in philosophy and grammar. The scientific senses of potential energy and electric potential follow in the 19th century.
items.cn: 英语 potential 于 17 世纪进入，最早用于哲学与语法。势能与电势的科学义则在 19 世纪跟进。

items.en: Modern English uses it for latent ability in people, for possible risks and customers, and for the technical quantities named after stored energy.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指人身上尚未显现的能力、可能的风险与客户，以及那些以储存能量命名的技术量。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root for being able. The second group collects words for what may happen and what is not yet developed.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“能够”的词根。第二组收表示“可能发生”与“尚未发展”的词。

entries.definition: possibly, in a way that may become real. It softens a claim: potentially dangerous means may be dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 可能地，以某种或将成真的方式。它使断言变软：potentially dangerous 意为“可能有危险”。

entries.definition: powerful or effective. Potent describes power already present; potential describes power not yet used.
entries.definitionCN: 强有力的、有效的。potent 描述已经在场的力；potential 描述尚未使用的力。

entries.definition: the state of being possible or having latent capacity. It is the philosophical noun built on potential.
entries.definitionCN: 处于可能状态或具有潜在能力。它是建立在 potential 之上的哲学名词。

entries.definition: all-powerful. Omni- 'all' plus potens 'able': able to do everything.
entries.definitionCN: 全能的。omni-“全部”加 potens“有能力的”：能做一切。

entries.definition: able to happen or be true. Possible is wider; potential often suggests a capacity that can be developed.
entries.definitionCN: 能够发生或为真。possible 更宽；potential 常暗示一种可以被发展出来的能力。

entries.definition: present but not yet active or visible. Latent stresses hiddenness; potential stresses capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 已存在但尚未活动或显现。latent 强调隐藏；potential 强调能力。

entries.definition: likely to happen or to become something in the future. Prospective is about the future position; potential is about the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 未来可能发生或成为的。prospective 关乎未来的位置；potential 关乎能力。

entries.definition: signs that someone or something will do well. Promise is the informal judgement; potential is the neutral capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某人或某物会出色的迹象。promise 是非正式的判断；potential 是中性的能力。

entries.definition: the amount something can hold or do. Capacity is measurable; potential can be unmeasured and unrealized.
entries.definitionCN: 某物能容纳或能做到的量。capacity 可测量；potential 可以未被测量、未被实现。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the drawn bow, the unseen champion, the water behind the dam, the battery terminal, and the coach's eye.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：拉开的弓、还没出头的冠军、坝后的水、电池两端、教练的眼光。

normal.en: Potential is a drawn bow: the force is already stored, only the release has not happened.
normal.cn: potential 是一张拉开的弓：力已经存好，只是还没放箭。

normal.en: A potential champion is someone whose trophy is still in the future.
normal.cn: a potential champion 是奖杯还在未来的人。

normal.en: Water held behind a dam is potential energy: high up, still, waiting.
normal.cn: 坝后存住的水就是势能：位置高、静止、等着。

normal.en: A battery keeps a potential difference: one terminal is higher than the other, and charge wants to flow down.
normal.cn: 电池维持电势差：一端比另一端高，电荷就想往下流。

normal.en: A coach sees potential, which means seeing the future player inside the present one.
normal.cn: 教练看到潜力，就是从现在这个球员身上看到未来的那个。

abstract.en: Potential is the gap between what is and what could be, and every measurement of it is a guess about the future.
abstract.cn: 潜力是“是什么”与“可能是什么”之间的落差，对它的每一次测量都是对未来的猜测。

abstract.en: Stored energy and undeveloped talent share one word because both are ability held in place.
abstract.cn: 储存的能量与未发展的才能共用一个词，因为两者都是被位置存住的“能够”。

abstract.en: Calling something potential is a way of praising it without yet committing to it.
abstract.cn: 称某物为 potential，是一种既赞美它、又尚未对它作出承诺的说法。

examples.en: The region has enormous potential for solar power.
examples.cn: 该地区在太阳能方面有巨大潜力。

examples.en: Investors were warned about the potential loss of their deposits.
examples.cn: 投资者被警告存款可能遭受损失。

examples.en: She never reached her full potential as a runner because of injuries.
examples.cn: 因为伤病，她从未跑出自己全部的潜力。

root: 拉丁语 posse“能够”（potis“有能力的”+ esse“是”）→ potens“有能力的”→ potentia“能力”→ 晚期拉丁 potentialis → 英语 potential（17 世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Everything turns on the difference between able-to-be and being. A possible event, an undeveloped talent, stored energy, a voltage, and a grammatical mood all describe capacity before it becomes act.
sensesIntro.cn: 一切都围绕“能够成为”与“已经成为”的差别。可能发生的事、未发展的才能、储存的能量、电压、语法语气，描述的都是“变成行动之前的能力”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretched bow held still, force stored and not yet released.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉满却静持的弓，力已储存，尚未放出。

branches.en: POSSIBILITY: what may happen, stated as an adjective and as a noun.
branches.cn: 可能性：可能发生之事，分别用形容词与名词表达。

branches.en: TALENT: capacity inside a person, seen by a coach or by the person herself.
branches.cn: 才能：人身上的能力，被教练或本人看见。

branches.en: STORED ENERGY: the bow, the dam, the lifted weight.
branches.cn: 储能：弓、坝、被举高的重物。

branches.en: ELECTRICITY: the level at a point and the difference between two points.
branches.cn: 电学：某点的电势与两点之间的电势差。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the form whose whole job is to say 'may be'.
branches.cn: 语法：专门负责说“可能是”的那个形式。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb for being able. Its participles and abstract nouns supply potent, potential, and potentiality; prefixes add scope such as all or many.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语表示“能够”的动词上。它的分词与抽象名词提供了 potent、potential、potentiality；前缀则加上“全部”“多”等范围。

latinIntro.en: Latin potens and potentia passed into English through scientific and philosophical writing, so the technical senses retain their Latin shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 potens 与 potentia 经科学与哲学写作进入英语，所以技术义仍保留拉丁形态。

senses.title: Possible but not actual
senses.titleCN: 潜在地：可能但还没发生
senses.definition: used to say that something may happen or may be true, without asserting that it does
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某事可能发生或可能成立，但不肯定它已经发生或成立
senses.example: The drug is potentially effective, but no trial has been completed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药可能有疗效，但还没有完成试验。
senses.why: potentia in Latin is 'power, capacity'. The adverb marks a capacity that exists before any result, so the statement stays open.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 potentia 是“力量、能力”。这个副词标记先于结果存在的能力，所以陈述保持开放。

senses.title: A latent power
senses.titleCN: 从潜力上看：能力还没释放
senses.definition: with respect to the capacity a person or thing still holds inside and has not yet used
senses.definitionCN: 从人或事物内部尚未释放的能力来看
senses.example: The team is potentially the strongest in the league.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在潜力上是联赛最强的。
senses.why: Here the word measures stored capacity rather than probability. The ranking is about what could be released, not about odds.
senses.whyCN: 这里它衡量的是储存的能力，而非概率。排名评的是可能释放的力量，不是赔率。

senses.title: Risk warning
senses.titleCN: 可能有危害：先提醒再说
senses.definition: used to flag a possible danger while leaving the certainty of that danger unstated
senses.definitionCN: 用于提示可能存在的危险，同时不说明危险的确定程度
senses.example: The chemical is potentially harmful to children.
senses.exampleCN: 这种化学物质可能对儿童有害。
senses.why: Risk language needs a word that names danger without proving it. The adverb lets a warning be urgent and still cautious.
senses.whyCN: 风险语言需要一个既指出危险又不证明危险的词。这个副词让警告既有紧迫感又保持谨慎。

senses.title: Tentative scientific claim
senses.definition: in scientific writing, used to report an inference whose evidence is indirect
senses.definitionCN: 在科学写作中，用于报告证据为间接的推论
senses.example: The pattern is potentially caused by a shift in ocean currents.
senses.exampleCN: 这一模式可能是由洋流变化造成的。
senses.why: Science separates observation from explanation. The adverb marks the step from data to a proposed cause, which is exactly where certainty drops.
senses.whyCN: 科学要把观察与解释分开。这个副词标记从数据迈到所提原因的那一步，而确定性正在这一步下降。

senses.title: Untapped resource
senses.titleCN: 可争取的资源：还没用上
senses.definition: describing a resource, market or worker whose value is available if it is used
senses.definitionCN: 描述资源、市场或劳动者只要被使用就有价值
senses.example: The region is potentially a major market for electric cars.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区可能成为电动汽车的重要市场。
senses.why: Economics uses the word for value that exists in possibility. The resource is real; only its use is missing.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用它指存在于可能性中的价值。资源是真实的，缺的只是使用。

senses.title: Mathematics and physics
senses.definition: in physics, describing a quantity defined at a point and realized only when something moves or changes
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学中描述某点上的量，只有发生移动或变化时才实现
senses.example: Energy is stored in the field as a potential difference.
senses.exampleCN: 能量以电势差的形式储存在场中。
senses.why: Physics gives the word its most literal sense: potential energy is energy by position, waiting for a release.
senses.whyCN: 物理学给了这个词最字面的义项：势能是按位置拥有的能量，等着被释放。

senses.title: Hedging in argument
senses.definition: used in debate to weaken a claim so that it cannot be refuted too easily
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论中用来弱化主张，使其不易被轻易驳倒
senses.example: This approach is potentially more fair, though the data are thin.
senses.exampleCN: 这一做法可能更公平，尽管数据很少。
senses.why: The adverb is a hedge: it transfers the burden of proof from the speaker to future evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是一种模糊限制：把举证责任从说话人转给未来的证据。

senses.title: Possibility in grammar
senses.definition: in grammar teaching, labelling an adverb that expresses possibility rather than certainty
senses.definitionCN: 在语法教学中标记表达可能性而非确定性的副词
senses.example: Potentially is a possibility adverb, like perhaps and conceivably.
senses.exampleCN: potentially 是可能性副词，与“也许”“可以想象地”等词同类。
senses.why: Grammar groups words by what they do to a sentence's certainty. This adverb lowers certainty without cancelling the statement.
senses.whyCN: 语法按“对句子确定性的作用”给词分组。这个副词降低确定性，但不取消陈述。

intro.en: Potentially is potential plus -ly. Potential comes from Latin potentia 'power, ability', from potens 'able, powerful', itself the present participle of posse 'to be able'.
intro.cn: potentially 是 potential 加 -ly。potential 来自拉丁语 potentia“力量、能力”，源于 potens“有能力的”，而 potens 是 posse“能够”的现在分词。

items.en: posse 'to be able' is a contraction of potis esse 'to be able'. potis is an old adjective meaning 'able, capable'.
items.cn: posse“能够”是 potis esse“有能力存在”的缩合。potis 是古形容词，意为“有能力的”。

items.en: The present participle potens 'being able' produced the adjective 'powerful'. From it English takes potent and potency.
items.cn: 现在分词 potens“有能力的”产生形容词“强有力的”。英语由此取得 potent 与 potency。

items.en: potentia abstracted the adjective into a noun: 'power, capacity, force'. The noun could mean capacity in the sense of what a thing can become.
items.cn: potentia 把形容词抽象为名词：力量、能力、势力。该名词也可指事物可能成为的那种“能力”。

items.en: English forms potential in the 14th century as an adjective from the Latin stem. The noun use 'capacity for future success' appears later.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪以拉丁词干构成形容词 potential。指“未来成功的潜力”的名词用法出现较晚。

items.en: The -ly adverb is formed on the adjective and spreads in scientific and journalistic prose, where claims need hedging.
items.cn: -ly 副词由该形容词构成，在科学与新闻写作中扩散，因为这些文体需要为论断留余地。

items.en: Physics fixes the meaning in potential energy and potential difference, where the quantity is real but unrealized.
items.cn: 物理学在势能与电势差中固定了词义：该量真实存在但尚未实现。

note.en: The look-alike group all contains pot- from potis or from a different root; the near-meaning group shares the idea of possibility but differs in strength.
note.cn: 形近组都含 pot-，或同出 potis，或另有来源；近义组都表“可能”，差别在可能性强度。

entries.definition: existing as a capacity rather than as an act. The adjective modifies a noun; the adverb modifies a whole claim.
entries.definitionCN: 潜在的；潜力。形容词修饰名词，副词修饰整个论断。

entries.definition: strong in effect, especially of a drug or argument. It states present power, not future possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 强效的；有力的。它陈述当下的力量，不是未来的可能。

entries.definition: safe to drink. It looks close but comes from Latin potare 'to drink', not from posse.
entries.definitionCN: 可饮用的。它外形接近，但来自拉丁 potare“喝”，并非 posse。

entries.definition: perhaps; used for plain uncertainty. It is more neutral and less technical than potentially.
entries.definitionCN: 也许；可能。用于一般的不确定，比 potentially 更中性、更少术语色彩。

entries.definition: in a way that can be imagined even if unlikely. It often signals a distant possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 可以想象地。即使不太可能也能想到，常暗示较远的可能性。

entries.definition: as may reasonably be supposed. It reports an inference from evidence, not a bare possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 大概；据推测。它报告基于证据的推断，不是单纯的可能。

entries.definition: as can be supported by argument. It hedges a judgment, while potentially hedges a prediction.
entries.definitionCN: 可以说是。它为判断留余地，而 potentially 为预测留余地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: potent- is the stem of 'having power', so potentially means 'with power still held in reserve'.
normal.cn: potent- 是“有力量”的词干，所以 potentially 意为“力量还握在手里未用”。

normal.en: Potential energy in physics is the cleanest model: the energy is there, the movement has not started.
normal.cn: 物理学的势能是最清楚的模型：能量在那里，运动还没开始。

normal.en: In warnings, potentially harmful and potentially fatal pair with the same hedging job.
normal.cn: 在警示语中，可能有危害与可能致命承担同样的留余地功能。

normal.en: Potential plus -ly keeps the adjective visible, so the adverb never claims more than the adjective does.
normal.cn: potential 加 -ly 仍看得见形容词，所以副词声称的绝不超过形容词。

normal.en: The paired noun is potential: a player with potential is one whose value is not yet shown.
normal.cn: 对应名词是 potential：有潜力的选手就是价值尚未展现的人。

abstract.en: Picture a seed in a drawer: the tree is fully possible and completely absent at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里的一颗种子：那棵树既完全可能，又完全不在。

abstract.en: Picture a door that is unlocked but has never been opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没锁、却从未被推开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a battery on a shelf: voltage is present, current is not flowing.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上的一节电池：电压在，电流没走。

examples.en: The virus is potentially more contagious than earlier variants.
examples.cn: 这种病毒可能比早期变种更具传染性。

examples.en: She is potentially the best candidate, but she has not applied.
examples.cn: 她可能是最佳人选，但她还没申请。

examples.en: Potentially, the new method could cut costs by a third.
examples.cn: 从可能性上说，新方法能把成本削减三分之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破摊子里”音近 potentially：破摊子里也许藏着好东西——只是“有可能” → potentially 潜在地

root: 拉丁 posse“能够”（potis esse 的缩合）→ potens“有能力的”→ potentia“力量、能力”；potential + -ly 构成副词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lower the certainty of a statement while keeping the thing described fully real.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在降低陈述的确定性，同时让所描述之物保持真实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed holding a tree that has not grown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗种子，里面装着还没长出的树。

branches.en: HEDGING: the everyday possibility claim and the debater's hedge both keep the statement open to revision.
branches.cn: 留余地：日常的可能性陈述与辩论中的模糊限制，都让论断保留修改空间。

branches.en: CAPACITY HELD: a strong team and an unused market are both value that exists before it is spent.
branches.cn: 握有的能力：强队与未开发市场都是尚未花掉就已存在的价值。

branches.en: WARNING: risk language names a danger without having to prove it.
branches.cn: 警示：风险语言指出危险，而不必先证明危险。

branches.en: GRAMMATICAL STANCE: scientific inference and grammar teaching both treat the word as a marker of lowered certainty.
branches.cn: 语法立场：科学推论与语法教学都把这个词当作降低确定性的标记。

branches.en: PHYSICS: potential energy and potential difference give the metaphor a measurable form.
branches.cn: 物理学：势能与电势差给这个比喻一个可测量的形态。

intro.en: Potentially is built from the Latin stem potent- plus the English suffix -ly. The -ia and -ia/-cy nouns and the -ent adjective belong to the same family.
intro.cn: potentially 由拉丁词干 potent- 加英语后缀 -ly 构成。-ia 名词、-cy 名词与 -ent 形容词同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin connects potis 'able' to posse 'be able' and potens 'able', from which potentia and English potent derive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把 potis“有能力的”、posse“能够”、potens“有能力的”串起来，potentia 与英语 potent 由此而来。

items.meaningCN: 潜在的；潜力（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: We have a potential buyer for the site.
items.exampleCN: 这块地有一位潜在买家。

items.meaningCN: 潜在地；有可能地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 这一变化可能意义重大。

items.meaningCN: 强效的；有力的（分词词干作形容词）

items.example: The potency of the drug declines with heat.

items.meaning: to increase the effect of something
items.meaningCN: 增强药效（-iate 动词后缀）
items.exampleCN: 该化合物增强了抗生素的效果。

items.example: The agency was impotent against the cartel.
items.exampleCN: 该机构对这个卡特尔无能为力。

items.example: The novel gives its ruler omnipotent powers.
items.exampleCN: 小说赋予统治者全能的力量。

items.meaning: dominant in inheritance, a genetics term
items.meaningCN: 遗传上优先显性的（pre-“在前”+ potent）
items.example: A prepotent gene masks the weaker one.
items.exampleCN: 优先显性的基因会掩盖较弱的那一个。

latinEntries.meaning: to be able, to have power

definition_en: the British unit of money; a unit of weight; to strike something hard and repeatedly; to beat with a heavy rhythm; and to crush something into a soft mass
core_image: 旧木桌上摊着一把硬币和一杆老秤，秤盘被压得往下沉

sceneCN: 这里 pound 指「英镑」（第 1 个义项：英国的货币单位）；句意为她花三英镑买下那杆黄铜秤，装进袋子带回家。图中可辨识场景：摊开在木桌上的硬币、被压低的秤盘、收摊前零乱的摊位。

猛击；砰砰地敲；捣碎

collocations.zh: 按同等重量相比；同等水平下

derivatives.zh: 由 pound 加 -ing 构成，义为「重击；砰砰的响声」

senses.title: The British unit of money
senses.definition: the standard unit of money in Britain, divided into one hundred pence
senses.definitionCN: 英国的标准货币单位，一英镑分为一百便士
senses.example: The ticket cost twenty pounds, which was more than he expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这张票要二十英镑，比他预想的多。
senses.why: English took the name of a weight for silver and used it for the money made of that weight, so the currency still carries a scale inside its name.
senses.whyCN: 英语把称银子用的重量名直接拿来指那个重量的银子所铸的钱，所以这种货币的名字里至今藏着一杆秤。

senses.title: A unit of weight
senses.definition: a unit of weight equal to about 454 grams, used in Britain and the United States
senses.definitionCN: 约合四百五十四克的重量单位，通行于英国与美国
senses.example: The recipe asks for two pounds of potatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份食谱要两磅土豆。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense in English: Old English pund weighed goods at the market long before it counted coins at the bank.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最老的义项：古英语 pund 早在银行数钱之前，就已经在市场上称货物了。

senses.title: To strike something hard and repeatedly
senses.definition: to hit something again and again with great force, usually with the fists or a heavy tool
senses.definitionCN: 用拳头或沉重工具反复用力击打某物
senses.example: He pounded the door until someone opened it.
senses.exampleCN: 他不停地擂门，直到有人来开。
senses.why: The beating verb is a separate Old English word, punian, probably imitative of blows; its spelling later merged with the weight word, but the force is its own.
senses.whyCN: 表示击打的动词另有来历，是古英语 punian，一般认为模仿打人的声响；后来拼写与重量词合流，但那股力道是它自带的。

senses.title: To beat with a heavy rhythm
senses.definition: to move or beat with a strong regular force, as a heart or a pair of running feet does
senses.definitionCN: 心脏或奔跑的脚步以强烈而规律的力道跳动、起落
senses.example: Her heart was pounding as she waited for the result.
senses.exampleCN: 等结果的时候，她的心怦怦直跳。
senses.why: Once the verb names repeated heavy blows, the body's own drum can borrow it, because a racing heart is felt as something striking from inside.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦指反复的重击，身体自己的鼓点就能借用它，因为心跳加速时，人感到的正是有什么在体内一下下撞。

senses.title: To crush something into a paste
senses.definition: to break something into small pieces or a soft mass by hitting it again and again in a mortar
senses.definitionCN: 用杵在臼里反复捶打，把东西碎成小块或软糊
senses.example: Pound the garlic with a little salt before adding the oil.
senses.exampleCN: 加橄榄油之前，先把蒜加一点盐捣碎。
senses.why: Crushing with a pestle is the same downward blow repeated in one small bowl, so the cooking sense keeps the action and changes only the result.
senses.whyCN: 用杵捣东西，就是在小臼里重复同一种向下砸的动作；烹饪义保留了动作，只换了结果。

intro.en: Pound carries two histories that ended up spelled alike: a Latin weight word that became money and mass, and an Old English verb of beating that probably copies the sound of blows.
intro.cn: pound 背着两段最后拼成同一个样子的历史：一个变成货币与重量的拉丁称重词，和一个很可能模仿打击声的古英语动词。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang and also to weigh, since goods were weighed on a hanging balance.
items.cn: pendere 既指悬挂，也指称重，因为货物是挂在秤上称的。

items.en: Pondo, short for libra pondo, meant a pound by weight, and this is the form that gave English the name of the unit.
items.cn: pondo 是 libra pondo 的省略，意为「按重量计的一磅」，英语里这个单位的名字就来自它。

items.en: Libra named both the scales and the Roman pound; its abbreviation lb and the crossed L of the money sign still stand for weight and for sterling.
items.cn: libra 既指天平，也指罗马磅；它的缩写 lb 与货币符号里那个带横杠的 L，至今仍分别代表重量与英镑。

items.en: Old English pund took the Latin weight word and used it for goods on the market and for silver by weight.
items.cn: 古英语 pund 接过这个拉丁重量词，既用于市场上的货物，也用于按重量计的银子。

items.en: A separate verb punian meant to beat or crush, probably imitative; Middle English merged its spelling with pound.
items.cn: 另有一个动词 punian，意为捶打、捣碎，一般认为带拟声性质；中古英语把它的拼写并入了 pound。

items.en: Modern English keeps the amount, the coin, the blows, the heartbeat and the mortar, all under five letters.
items.cn: 现代英语把这几种意思都留在五个字母里：分量、钱币、捶打、心跳与捣臼。

note.en: The look-alike group puts the word's own derivatives beside two spellings that only resemble it; the near-meaning group gathers money words and verbs of beating.
note.cn: 形近组把本词自己的派生词与两个只是拼写相像的词放在一起；近义组收货币词与表示捶打的动词。

entries.definition: Something that weighs or hits a stated number of pounds.
entries.definitionCN: 重达若干磅的东西；捣击者。

entries.definition: Weight measured in pounds, or a charge made by weight.
entries.definitionCN: 以磅计的重量；按重量收取的费用。

entries.definition: To jump on something suddenly and seize it, as a cat does.
entries.definitionCN: 突然扑上去抓住，如猫扑猎物；这只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To push the lips forward in displeasure.
entries.definitionCN: 不高兴地撅起嘴唇；这只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: British money of standard purity, especially the pound.
entries.definitionCN: 标准纯度的英国货币，尤指英镑。

entries.definition: To hit something heavily, making a dull sound.
entries.definitionCN: 重重地打，发出闷响。

entries.definition: To strike again and again in a regular rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 以规律节奏反复打击。

entries.definition: To hit something hard with a tool or with force.
entries.definitionCN: 用工具或用力反复敲打。

normalIntro.en: Two strands meet in one spelling: a weighed amount that became money, and a repeated blow that became a heartbeat and a mortar.
normalIntro.cn: 两条线在一个拼写里相遇：一个被称出来的分量变成了钱，一种反复的击打变成了心跳与捣臼。

normal.en: Libra is why the abbreviation lb stands for a pound of weight and why the money sign carries a crossed L.
normal.cn: 正因为 libra，重量单位缩写写作 lb，货币符号里也带着一个带横杠的 L。

normal.en: Pondo meant by weight, so a pound was first a quantity of silver, and only later the coin made from it.
normal.cn: pondo 意为「按重量计」，所以一磅最早是一份银子，后来才指用这份银子铸的钱。

normal.en: The beating pound is a different word, from Old English punian, so no weight is hidden inside pound the door.
normal.cn: 表示捶打的 pound 是另一个词，出自古英语 punian，所以「擂门」那个 pound 里并没有藏着重量的意思。

normal.en: Compare heart pounding and rain pounding on the roof: both describe a heavy rhythm rather than a single blow.
normal.cn: 比较 heart pounding 与雨打屋顶：两者说的都是有节奏的重击，而不是单独一下。

normal.en: Pound the garlic names the same downward stroke a pestle makes in a mortar.
normal.cn: pound the garlic 说的正是杵在臼里那一下下的下砸动作。

abstract.en: A currency named after a weight reminds you that money once had to be put on a scale.
abstract.cn: 一种以重量命名的货币提醒人：钱曾经必须放上秤。

abstract.en: The word holds a scale and a hammer at once, and context decides which one you are holding.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时握着一杆秤和一把锤子，语境决定你手里拿的是哪一样。

abstract.en: A heart pounds in the same rhythm as a fist on a door, which is why one verb serves both.
abstract.cn: 心跳与拳头擂门是同一种节奏，所以一个动词能同时管这两件事。

examples.en: She paid three pounds for the brass scales.
examples.cn: 她花三英镑买下了那杆黄铜秤。

examples.en: He pounded the garlic with a little salt.
examples.cn: 他把蒜加一点盐捣碎。

examples.en: Her heart pounded as the plane touched down.
examples.cn: 飞机落地时，她的心怦怦直跳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「磅」的读音正好对得上；一磅重的东西砸下来砰的一声，pound 既是磅与英镑，也是猛砸。

root: 重量与货币义来自拉丁语 libra pondo（按重量计的一磅），经古英语 pund 进入英语；猛击义另有来源，一般认为出自古英语 punian（捶打、捣碎），可能为拟声。

sensesIntro.en: The senses split into two groups: a measured amount that turned into money, and a repeated heavy blow that turned into a heartbeat and a pestle.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项分成两群：一个被称出来的分量变成了钱，一种反复的重击变成了心跳与杵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass balance on an old table, its pan pressed low by a heap of coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧木桌上一杆黄铜秤，秤盘被一堆硬币压得很低。

branches.en: coins counted twice on a market stall
branches.cn: 摊位上被数了两遍的硬币

branches.en: potatoes dropping one by one onto a scale
branches.cn: 土豆一个个落到秤盘上

branches.en: a fist landing on a locked door
branches.cn: 拳头一下下砸在锁着的门上

branches.en: a pulse felt in the throat while waiting
branches.cn: 等候时喉咙里感到的脉搏

branches.en: a pestle turning garlic into paste
branches.cn: 杵把蒜捣成糊

intro.en: A Latin family of weighing supplies the money and the mass, while the beating verb comes from Old English; English suffixes then build the noise, the tool and the charge.
intro.cn: 一个表示称重的拉丁词族提供了货币与质量义，表示击打的动词则来自古英语；英语后缀再分别造出响声、器具与按磅计的收费。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a unit of weight or money
weight or charge measured in pounds

definition_zh: 倒；灌；倾泻；大量涌入；倾诉；浇筑
definition_en: to make a liquid flow out of a container, to cause people or things to move in a steady stream, to rain very heavily, to tell feelings freely, or to cast wet concrete
core_image: 一只手把壶嘴压低，水柱落进杯里，杯口腾起一点热气
scene: 屋檐下的水线连成一片，院里的人抱着盆往外泼。It had poured all night, and the lane was ankle-deep in water.
sceneCN: 这里 pour 指「大雨倾盆而下」（第 3 个义项：雨下得又急又密）；句意为雨下了一整夜，巷子里的水已经没到脚踝。图中可辨识场景：连成水线的屋檐、往外泼水的盆、漫过路面的积水。

pos.zh: 倒；灌；倾泻；涌入；倾诉；浇筑

derivatives.zh: 由 down 与 pour 复合而成，义为「倾盆大雨」
由 out 与 pouring 复合而成，义为「倾泻；情感的流露」
由 pour 加表示人或物的 -er 构成，义为「倒液体的人或器具」

senses.title: To make a liquid flow from a container
senses.definition: to hold a container at an angle so that the liquid inside runs out into another vessel
senses.definitionCN: 把容器倾斜，让里面的液体流进另一个器皿
senses.example: She poured the tea slowly so that the leaves stayed in the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 她慢慢地倒茶，让茶叶留在壶里。
senses.why: The oldest recorded use is simply liquid leaving a vessel, and every later sense keeps that picture of something flowing out under control.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早用法就是液体离开容器，后来每个义项都保留着这幅画面：有东西在控制之下流出来。

senses.title: To move in a continuous stream
senses.definition: to come or go somewhere in large numbers and without a break, like a liquid that will not stop
senses.definitionCN: 像止不住的液体一样，大批而不间断地来或去
senses.example: Fans poured out of the stadium as the final whistle blew.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响，球迷从体育场里涌了出来。
senses.why: A crowd moves like a liquid when it is dense enough, so English uses the same verb for people, letters and money arriving in an unbroken flow.
senses.whyCN: 人群一旦密集，移动起来就像液体，于是英语用同一个动词来说人、信件和钱源源不断地到来。

senses.title: To rain very heavily
senses.definition: to rain hard and steadily, so that water seems to be tipped out of the sky
senses.definitionCN: 雨下得又急又密，仿佛天上有水被整盆倒下
senses.example: It poured all afternoon, and nobody left the house.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午都在下倾盆大雨，谁也没出门。
senses.why: Rain is water falling in sheets, so the verb of tipping out a vessel transfers to the sky itself, especially in the impersonal phrase it is pouring.
senses.whyCN: 雨就是成片落下的水，于是「把容器倒空」的动词被挪到天上，尤其在 it is pouring 这种无人称说法里。

senses.title: To tell feelings without holding back
senses.definition: to express feelings or a story freely and at length, as if emptying what is inside
senses.definitionCN: 把心里的感受或经历毫无保留地、连续地说出来
senses.example: She poured out the whole story to a friend at the kitchen table.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在厨房桌边，把整件事都向朋友倾诉了出来。
senses.why: If a vessel can be emptied, so can a person, and pour out turns the chest into a container whose contents finally leave.
senses.whyCN: 容器能被倒空，人也可以；pour out 把胸腔变成一只容器，里面的东西终于流了出来。

senses.title: To cast wet concrete or metal
senses.definition: to fill a mould or a prepared space with wet concrete or molten metal so that it sets into shape
senses.definitionCN: 把湿混凝土或熔化的金属灌进模子或备好的空间，让它凝固成形
senses.example: The crew poured the foundation before the rain came.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在下雨之前浇好了地基。
senses.why: Building work borrows the kitchen verb because wet concrete is a heavy liquid that has to be tipped into a prepared shape and left to harden.
senses.whyCN: 建筑行当借用这个厨房动词，因为湿混凝土就是一种沉重的液体，要倒进备好的形状里，再等它变硬。

intro.en: Pour is a Middle English verb whose origin is uncertain. The usual guess points to Old French, but no link has been proved, and the word has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: pour 是中古英语的一个动词，来源不确定。常见的猜测指向古法语，但没有得到证实，这个词也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: Pour first appears around the fourteenth century as pouren, meaning to flow, gush or tip liquid out; the earlier history is not recorded.
items.cn: pour 约在十四世纪以 pouren 的形式出现，意为流出、涌出、把液体倒出；更早的来历没有记录。

items.en: Some dictionaries suggest a link with Old French purer, to pour out or strain, but the connection remains a guess rather than an established borrowing.
items.cn: 有些词典猜测它与古法语 purer（倒出、滤出）有关，但这只是一种猜测，并未确立为借词关系。

items.en: The verb widened from liquid in a cup to crowds leaving a gate and to rain falling in sheets, because all three move in one unbroken flow.
items.cn: 这个动词从杯里的液体扩展到涌出大门的人群与成片落下的雨，因为三者都是不间断地流动。

items.en: With modern building work the verb took on concrete and metal, which are liquids only until they set.
items.cn: 随着近代建筑工程，这个动词用到了混凝土与金属上，而它们只在凝固之前是液体。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense and adds the emotional one, so a person may pour tea, pour out a story, or stand in the pouring rain.
items.cn: 现代英语保留物理义，又添了情感义，所以一个人可以倒茶、倾诉一件事，也可以站在倾盆大雨里。

note.en: The look-alike group puts two spellings that merely sound the same beside the word's own derivatives; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for liquid on the move.
note.cn: 形近组把两个只是读音相同的拼写与本词自己的派生词放在一起；近义组收表示液体流动的动词。

entries.definition: A tiny opening in skin or in a leaf; also to study a text closely.
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤或叶片上的小孔；也指细读；这只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having little money or little quality.
entries.definitionCN: 缺钱的；质量差的；这只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person or vessel that pours liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 倒液体的人或器具。

entries.definition: A sudden heavy fall of rain.
entries.definitionCN: 突如其来的倾盆大雨。

entries.definition: To let liquid fall out of a container by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 不慎让液体从容器里洒出。

entries.definition: To move steadily and smoothly, as a liquid does.
entries.definitionCN: 像液体一样平稳不断地移动。

entries.definition: To move in a continuous current.
entries.definitionCN: 以连续的水流般移动。

entries.definition: To flow out suddenly and in large amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 突然大量涌出。

normalIntro.en: There is no Latin root to lean on here, so the word is best held by its pictures: a tipped jug, a crowd at a gate, a sky emptied out.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁词根可依靠，最好用画面来记住它：倾斜的壶、门口的人群、被倒空的天。

normal.en: Pour out and pour into are the two directions: out of a container, into another place or crowd.
normal.cn: pour out 与 pour into 是两个方向：从容器里出来，进入另一个地方或人群。

normal.en: Downpour adds down to pour, and English rain does fall down, so the compound needs no explanation.
normal.cn: downpour 在 pour 前加 down，英语的雨本来就是往下落的，所以这个复合词不必多解释。

normal.en: Outpouring keeps the same movement for feelings: what was inside comes out in quantity.
normal.cn: outpouring 把同一种流动用在情感上：原本在里面的东西大量地出来了。

normal.en: Pourer adds -er, so the word can name a person or a jug designed to pour cleanly.
normal.cn: pourer 加 -er，于是这个词既能指人，也能指专门设计来倒得干净的壶。

normal.en: It is pouring is impersonal, like it is raining: the sky, not a person, is doing the pouring.
normal.cn: it is pouring 是无人称句，和 it is raining 一样：倒水的是天，不是人。

abstract.en: Pour is what happens when a boundary is opened: a jug, a gate, a heart, a mould.
abstract.cn: pour 说的是边界被打开的那一刻：壶口、门口、心口、模子口。

abstract.en: The same verb covers tea and rain because both are water that has stopped being held.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词能管茶也能管雨，因为两者都是不再被兜住的水。

abstract.en: To pour out a story is to treat words as something liquid and finite, stored until it runs.
abstract.cn: 把故事倾诉出来，就是把话语当成一种有限的水，一直存着，直到流尽。

examples.en: She poured the tea slowly into four cups.
examples.cn: 她把茶慢慢倒进四只杯子里。

examples.en: It poured all night and the lane flooded.
examples.cn: 雨下了一整夜，巷子都淹了。

examples.en: He poured out his worries to an old friend.
examples.cn: 他把心里的烦恼向一位老朋友倾诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼」——泼水出去就是 pour；雨大得整盆往下倒，也说 it is pouring。

root: 中古英语 pouren（涌出、倾倒），约十四世纪见于记录，更早来源不确定；有词典猜测与古法语 purer（倒出、滤出）有关，但未成定论，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The senses all describe something leaving a boundary in a steady flow: liquid, a crowd, rain, feeling, wet concrete.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项说的都是某种东西越过边界、连续流出：液体、人群、雨、情感、湿混凝土。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tipping a jug lower, a thin column of water dropping into a cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把壶压得更低，一条细水柱落进杯里。

branches.en: a teapot tilted until the last drop leaves
branches.cn: 茶壶被倾到最后一滴流出

branches.en: a gate opening onto a river of people
branches.cn: 大门打开，人群像河水涌出

branches.en: a gutter overflowing while the sky stays grey
branches.cn: 天还灰着，排水沟已经溢出

branches.en: words coming faster than the listener can nod
branches.cn: 话说得比听的人点头还快

branches.en: wet concrete sliding down a wooden form
branches.cn: 湿混凝土顺着木模滑下

intro.en: With no Latin stem behind it, the word is held together by English pieces: the base verb, its participles, -er for the vessel, and the compounds down and out.
intro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁词干，靠英语自身的部件撑起来：基础动词、它的分词、表示器具的 -er，以及 down 与 out 两个复合成分。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a person or vessel that pours
a flood of feeling or of people

definition_zh: 贫穷；贫困；缺乏钱财与基本生活资源的状态；也指某种东西的匮乏或贫瘠
definition_en: the state of being extremely poor, lacking the money and resources needed for basic living; also a general scarcity or barrenness
core_image: 一只空碗放在缺了角的桌上，窗外的田里只长着稀疏的草，屋里屋外都显出「不够」
scene: 救济站里的登记表写满了名字，很多人连过冬的煤都买不起。The charity works to reduce poverty among families in the river valley.
sceneCN: 此处指「缺乏钱财与基本生活资源的状态」（第 1 个义项：缺钱维持基本生活）；句意为这家慈善机构致力于减轻河谷家庭的贫困。图中可辨识物件：空碗、破桌、稀疏的田草、救济登记表；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 贫穷；贫困（缺乏基本生活资源的状态）
匮乏；贫瘠（某种东西数量少或质量差）

forms.label: 复数（罕见，指多种贫困状况）

derivatives.zh: 贫穷的；差的
差地；身体不适地
使贫穷；使贫瘠
贫困的；贫瘠的
贫困化；贫瘠化
饱受贫困之苦的

senses.title: Lack of money for basic needs
senses.definition: the condition of not having enough money to pay for food, shelter, clothing and health care
senses.definitionCN: 没有足够的钱支付食物、住房、衣着与医疗
senses.example: Half the village lives in poverty and often skips meals.
senses.exampleCN: 村里一半人生活在贫困中，常常省掉饭食。
senses.why: The word names a shortage of the means of living, so its core sense is money that does not stretch to necessities.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是维生手段的短缺，因此核心义就是钱不足以覆盖基本需要。

senses.title: The state of being poor
senses.definition: the ongoing social condition of being poor, with its insecurity and limited choices
senses.definitionCN: 长期处于贫穷的社会状态，伴随不安全与选择受限
senses.example: Poverty traps families in unsafe housing and unstable work.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困把家庭困在不安全的住房与不稳定的工作里。
senses.why: Poverty is not only a moment of shortage but a condition that persists and shapes a life.
senses.whyCN: 贫困不只是一时的短缺，而是一种持续并塑造生活的状态。

senses.title: Officially measured deprivation
senses.definition: the level of deprivation defined by income falling below a government or research threshold
senses.definitionCN: 以收入低于政府或研究机构设定的门槛来界定的匮乏程度
senses.example: The census reports poverty by counting households below the threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查通过统计低于门槛的家庭来报告贫困。
senses.why: Modern states turned an old condition into a number by drawing a line and counting who falls under it.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家画一条线、数清线下人数，把古老的处境变成了数字。

senses.title: Scarcity of a resource
senses.definition: a serious shortage of something needed, such as water, soil nutrients or energy
senses.definitionCN: 水、土壤养分或能源等必需品严重不足
senses.example: Poverty of rainfall kept the fields bare for months.
senses.exampleCN: 降雨稀少让田地空了好几个月。
senses.why: The idea of having too little extends from money to any resource, which gives the word its scarcity sense.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有的太少」这一想法从钱扩展到任何资源，于是有了短缺义。

senses.title: Barrenness or poor quality
senses.definition: the state of land or material being thin, worn out or lacking richness
senses.definitionCN: 土地或材料稀薄、耗竭、缺乏肥力的状态
senses.example: The poverty of the soil forced farmers to move every few years.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤贫瘠迫使农民每隔几年就迁移。
senses.why: Land that yields little looks poor in the same way a person with little money does, so the word describes thinness of quality.
senses.whyCN: 产出很少的土地，看起来就像缺钱的人一样「穷」，于是这个词也描述质地的贫薄。

senses.title: Lack of ideas or imagination
senses.definition: the quality of being unoriginal, thin or lacking intellectual substance
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏创意、内容单薄、思想贫乏的性质
senses.example: Critics attacked the poverty of the plan's imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击这份计划想象力的贫乏。
senses.why: If a field can be poor, so can an argument, and the metaphor of thinness carries over to thought.
senses.whyCN: 田地可以贫瘠，论证也可以，贫薄这个比喻就延伸到思想上。

senses.title: Voluntary humility in religious writing
senses.titleCN: 宗教写作中自愿的谦卑
senses.definition: the deliberate giving up of worldly wealth or self-importance, especially in religious tradition
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在宗教传统中，主动放弃世俗财富或自我重要感
senses.example: Monks took a vow of poverty and owned nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 修士立下守贫之愿，不拥有任何财物。
senses.why: Religious tradition reframed lack as a virtue when it is chosen, so poverty gained a voluntary, spiritual sense.
senses.whyCN: 宗教传统把自愿的缺乏重新解释为美德，于是贫困获得了自愿的、精神性的义项。

senses.title: Destitution and dependence on charity
senses.definition: the extreme end of poverty in which a person depends on begging or public relief to survive
senses.definitionCN: 贫困的极端一端，人靠乞讨或公共救济才能活下去
senses.example: The old poorhouse sheltered people reduced to poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的济贫院收容陷入赤贫的人。
senses.why: At its worst the condition leaves a person with nothing to sell but labour or appeal, and this is the destitution sense.
senses.whyCN: 到最严重时，人除了劳力或求助已无物可售，这就是赤贫义。

intro.en: Poverty comes from Latin paupertas, the abstract noun of pauper 'poor', through Old French. The deeper origin of pauper is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语来自拉丁语 paupertas，即 pauper「贫穷」的抽象名词。pauper 的更早来源未查明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pauper meant 'poor, needy'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to a root meaning 'produce little' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: pauper 意为「贫穷、匮乏」。其更深来源无定论；把它与表示「产出很少」的词根相联系的旧说只是假说。

items.en: Paupertas 'poverty, want' was the abstract noun, and it passed into Old French as poverte.
items.cn: paupertas「贫穷、匮乏」是对应的抽象名词，后来变成古法语的 poverte。

items.en: Old French poverte entered English in the thirteenth century, naming both the condition and the lack of goods.
items.cn: 古法语 poverte 于十三世纪进入英语，既指贫穷状态，也指物品的匮乏。

items.en: Religious writing used poverty of spirit for voluntary humility, a sense that survives in set phrases.
items.cn: 宗教文献用「精神上的贫穷」指自愿的谦卑，这一义项保留在固定说法里。

items.en: From the nineteenth century poverty became an object of social measurement, defined by income against a line.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，贫穷成为社会测量对象，以收入是否低于某条线来界定。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of pauper): no agreed Indo-European etymology exists, and the date of the abstract noun is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（pauper 的拉丁语之前来源）：没有公认的印欧语词源，抽象名词的年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close but come from other roots; group two holds words for hardship and shortage.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近却另有词源的词；第二组是表示困苦与短缺的词。

entries.definition: Property comes from Latin proprietas 'ownership', built on proprius 'one's own'; it has nothing to do with pauper.
entries.definitionCN: 财产来自拉丁 proprietas「所有权」，出自 proprius「自己的」，与 pauper 毫无关系。

entries.definition: Propriety also goes back to proprius and means correctness of behaviour, not lack of money.
entries.definitionCN: 礼节同样出自 proprius，指行为得体，与缺钱无关。

entries.definition: Paucity means a small number or amount and comes from Latin paucus 'few'; it is a near neighbour in meaning but not in root.
entries.definitionCN: 少量来自拉丁 paucus「少」，意思相近，词根却不同。

entries.definition: Poor is the everyday adjective related to poverty, but it comes through Old French povre from the same Latin pauper.
entries.definitionCN: poor 是与贫穷相关的日常形容词，经古法语 povre 来自同一个拉丁 pauper。

entries.definition: Destitution is poverty so severe that a person lacks food, shelter and any means of recovery.
entries.definitionCN: 赤贫是严重到缺乏食物、住所与任何恢复手段的贫困。

entries.definition: Deprivation stresses the absence of specific necessities such as heating, food or schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 匮乏强调取暖、食物或教育等具体必需品的缺失。

entries.definition: Hardship is suffering caused by difficult conditions, which may occur without absolute poverty.
entries.definitionCN: 困苦是艰难处境带来的痛苦，未必达到绝对贫困。

entries.definition: Scarcity is a short supply of a particular resource and is the general form of the resource sense.
entries.definitionCN: 稀缺指某种资源供应不足，是资源义的一般化形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin base, real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The Latin base means poor, and the abstract ending turns it into the state of being poor.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为贫穷，抽象后缀把它变成「贫穷的状态」。

normal.en: The everyday adjective and the formal noun belong to the same family.
normal.cn: 日常形容词与正式名词属于同一词族。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the measured sense: poverty line, relative poverty, extreme poverty.
normal.cn: 固定说法承载测量义：贫困线、相对贫困、极端贫困。

normal.en: The same word can describe thin soil or a thin argument, because both are forms of not having enough.
normal.cn: 同一个词既能形容贫瘠的土壤，也能形容单薄的论证，因为两者都是「不够」。

normal.en: Religious tradition added the voluntary sense: a vow of poverty is a choice, not a misfortune.
normal.cn: 宗教传统加上自愿义：守贫之愿是选择，而非不幸。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl that is always half empty, however often it is filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗，无论添多少次，总有一半是空的。

abstract.en: Picture a field that grows grass but never grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一块地只长草，从不结粮。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of furniture and still somehow bare.
abstract.cn: 想象一间堆满家具却仍显得空荡的屋子。

examples.en: The programme cut poverty among older people by raising the basic pension.
examples.cn: 该项目通过提高基本养老金减少了老年人的贫困。

examples.en: Poverty of data made the report's conclusions uncertain.
examples.cn: 数据的匮乏让报告的结论难以确定。

examples.en: She took a vow of poverty and gave away her inheritance.
examples.cn: 她立下守贫之愿，把继承的财产捐了出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破屋」——屋顶漏风、米缸见底，就是贫穷；记住「破」与「贫」的连带感

root: 拉丁 pauper「贫穷」经古法语进入英语，加上抽象名词后缀构成 paupertas「贫穷、匮乏」，再演变为今天的贫穷一词；pauper 的拉丁语之前来源不确定，相关词根联系多为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shortage: money is missing, then the condition persists, is counted, is extended to resources, to soil, to thought, to chosen humility and finally to total destitution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「短缺」展开：先是缺钱，继而状态持续、被计数，再扩展到资源、土壤、思想、自愿的谦卑，最后到一无所有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl on a broken table, with thin grass outside and an empty coal sack by the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：缺角桌上的空碗，窗外稀疏的草，门边空着的煤袋。

branches.en: THE SHORTAGE ITSELF: money is missing, and the lack settles into a lasting condition.
branches.cn: 短缺本身：钱不够，而且这种缺乏沉淀为持久状态。

branches.en: THE COUNT: a line is drawn and the condition becomes an official number.
branches.cn: 计数：画一条线，处境就变成官方数字。

branches.en: FROM MONEY TO MATERIAL: the same thinness describes a scarce resource and barren soil.
branches.cn: 从钱到物：同一种「薄」也能形容短缺的资源与贫瘠的土壤。

branches.en: THIN THOUGHT: an argument can be as poor as a field.
branches.cn: 单薄的思想：论证可以像田地一样贫瘠。

branches.en: CHOSEN AND TOTAL LACK: lack becomes a vow at one end and destitution at the other.
branches.cn: 自愿的与彻底的缺乏：一端是守贫之愿，另一端是赤贫。

intro.en: Poverty is a Latin abstract noun that grew a wide metaphorical reach in English, from money to soil to ideas.
intro.cn: 贫穷是一个拉丁抽象名词，在英语里长出了很宽的比喻范围，从金钱到土壤再到思想。

latinIntro.en: Pauper and paupertas supply the core; English added the adjective, the verb and several compounds.
latinIntro.cn: pauper 与 paupertas 提供核心，英语再加形容词、动词与若干复合词。

items.example: The soil was impoverished by years of planting.

items.example: Aid reached the poverty-stricken villages late.
items.exampleCN: 援助很晚才到达饱受贫困之苦的村庄。

items.example: A paucity of evidence weakened the case.

scene: 厨房的木案上，一块干姜被小刀刮下细屑，落进碗里。She stirred the ginger powder into the hot soup.

senses.title: A solid crushed into fine grains
senses.definition: a dry solid substance broken into very small grains, like dust
senses.definitionCN: 干燥的固体被弄成极细的颗粒，状如灰尘
senses.example: The mortar had been ground to a fine powder.
senses.exampleCN: 研钵里的东西已经被磨成细粉。
senses.why: Latin pulvis meant dust, so the word starts from the state a hard thing reaches after it is crushed, not from any particular material.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pulvis 意为灰尘，所以这个词的起点是硬物被碾碎之后达到的状态，而不是某种特定的材料。

senses.title: A product sold in this form
senses.definition: a household or food product made and sold as fine grains, such as a washing or milk powder
senses.definitionCN: 以细颗粒形态制造并出售的家用或食品用品，如洗衣粉、奶粉
senses.example: She added a scoop of milk powder to the warm water.
senses.exampleCN: 她往温水里加了一勺奶粉。
senses.why: Once the form has a name, the goods packed in that form borrow it, so the word moves from a texture to a whole class of products.
senses.whyCN: 这种形态一旦有了名字，装成这种形态出售的商品就借用了它，于是词义从一种质地转到一整类产品。

senses.title: The explosive used in guns
senses.definition: an explosive mixture of saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal, used to fire guns and cannon
senses.definitionCN: 硝石、硫磺和木炭混合成的爆炸物，用来发射枪炮
senses.example: The old fort stored barrels of powder in the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 旧要塞的地窖里存放着一桶桶火药。
senses.why: Gunpowder was the first powder that mattered in European daily life, so the bare word could stand for it alone; the compound gunpowder later made that clear.
senses.whyCN: 在欧洲日常生活中，火药是最早重要起来的一种粉，所以单说这个词就能指它；后来才用复合词 gunpowder 把这层意思说明白。

senses.title: Cosmetic dust for the skin
senses.definition: a fine cosmetic dust pressed or loose, used to make skin look smoother
senses.definitionCN: 细滑的化妆用粉，压成粉饼或散装，用来让皮肤看起来更匀净
senses.example: She patted powder onto her cheeks before the camera flashed.
senses.exampleCN: 闪光灯亮起前，她在脸颊上轻轻扑了粉。
senses.why: A face powder is simply the same material applied to skin, so the word narrows by context rather than by any new root.
senses.whyCN: 扑面粉不过是把同一种材料用到皮肤上，所以这一义项是靠语境收窄的，并没有换词根。

senses.title: To dust something with powder
senses.definition: to put powder on a surface or on the skin, usually in a thin layer
senses.definitionCN: 把粉薄薄地撒在某个表面或皮肤上
senses.example: He powdered the baby's skin before dressing her.
senses.exampleCN: 他给婴儿的皮肤扑了粉，再给她穿衣服。
senses.why: English often turns a mass noun into a verb without any ending, and to powder is exactly the act of applying the material the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把不可数名词直接当动词用，to powder 正是把名词所指的材料涂抹上去的动作。

intro.en: Powder is Latin dust filtered through French: pulvis became poudre, and English trimmed the spelling and widened the meaning.
intro.cn: powder 是拉丁语「灰尘」经法语滤过来的词：pulvis 变成 poudre，英语又简化了拼写并扩大了词义。

items.en: Pulvis meant dust or powder, and its stem pulver- carried the idea of something ground very fine.
items.cn: pulvis 意为灰尘、粉末，它的词干 pulver- 表示被磨得极细的东西。

items.en: The oblique form pulverem carried the word into popular Latin, and it is the shape behind the Romance words for dust.
items.cn: pulvis 的斜格形式 pulverem 把这个词带入通俗拉丁语，罗曼语族表示灰尘的词都从这一形式来。

items.en: Old French reduced the word to poudre, the everyday term for dust and for ground spices.
items.cn: 古法语把它简化成 poudre，是当时指灰尘与研磨香料粉的日常说法。

items.en: Middle English wrote it poudre or powder, first for dust and spices, then for the explosive that changed warfare.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 poudre 或 powder，先指灰尘和香料粉，后来也指改变战争方式的火药。

items.en: Modern English settled on powder and added washing powders, milk powders, face powder and the verb to powder.
items.cn: 现代英语定型为 powder，并添上洗衣粉、奶粉、扑面粉以及动词 to powder 等用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same Latin dust stem plus compounds; the near-meaning group gathers words for loose grains and fine material.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一拉丁「灰尘」词干上的形式与复合词；近义组收表示松散颗粒与细碎物质的词。

entries.definition: Like powder, or covered with a thin layer of fine dust.
entries.definitionCN: 由 powder 加 -y 构成，义为「粉状的；覆着细粉的」。

entries.definition: Made into powder or dusted with it, as in powdered sugar.
entries.definitionCN: 由 powder 加 -ed 构成，义为「制成粉的；撒了粉的」，如糖粉。

entries.definition: An explosive mixture of saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal, built from gun and powder.
entries.definitionCN: 由 gun 与 powder 复合，指硝石、硫磺与木炭混成的火药。

entries.definition: To crush something into dust, from the Latin stem pulver- that also stands behind powder.
entries.definitionCN: 与 powder 同出拉丁词干 pulver-，义为「把……碾成粉」。

entries.definition: Fine dry particles of earth or other matter that settle on surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 灰尘；指落在地面或物体表面的细土与碎屑。

entries.definition: A single small hard particle of a substance such as sand or salt.
entries.definitionCN: 颗粒；指沙、盐等物质的一粒小硬粒。

entries.definition: A small grain, often one of many pressed together into a larger form.
entries.definitionCN: 小颗粒；常指压成较大形状的许多小粒之一。

entries.definition: Grain ground into a fine powder and used for baking.
entries.definitionCN: 面粉；指磨成细粉的谷物，专用于烘焙。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin dust in English clothes, and its family keeps returning to crushed solids, packed goods and the act of dusting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是穿上英语外衣的拉丁语「灰尘」，同族词反复回到碾碎的固体、包装出售的货品与撒粉的动作。

normal.en: Powder comes from Latin pulvis, dust, so the original idea is matter reduced to grains too small to hold.
normal.cn: powder 来自拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘），原意是被弄成小到抓不住的颗粒的物质。

normal.en: Old French kept the word as poudre, and English simply dropped the u in the spelling.
normal.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 poudre，英语只是把拼写里的 u 去掉了。

normal.en: Powdery adds -y and describes anything that looks or feels like powder.
normal.cn: powdery 加 -y，用来形容看起来或摸起来像粉的东西。

normal.en: Gunpowder is gun plus powder, which is why the bare word can still mean the explosive in older writing.
normal.cn: gunpowder 是 gun 加 powder，所以在较早的文字里单说 powder 仍可指火药。

normal.en: Washing powder and milk powder are named for their form, not for what they contain.
normal.cn: 洗衣粉与奶粉是按形态命名的，不是按成分命名的。

abstract.en: A solid loses its shape when it becomes powder, so the word sits halfway between a substance and its dust.
abstract.cn: 固体变成粉就失去了形状，所以这个词停在「物质」与「它的尘」之间。

abstract.en: The same dust can feed a baby, clean a shirt or blow down a wall, and English keeps one word for all three.
abstract.cn: 同一种粉可以喂婴儿、洗衣服或炸塌一堵墙，英语对这三件事只用一个词。

abstract.en: To powder a face is to add a layer thin enough to look like nothing at all.
abstract.cn: 给脸扑粉，是加上薄到看不出的一层。
