senses.title: Physical force
senses.definition: the strength or energy that something uses to move, break or hold another thing
senses.definitionCN: 某物用于移动、破坏或固定另一物的力量或能量
senses.example: The storm's power tore the roof from the shed.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴的力量把棚屋的屋顶掀掉了。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'to be able'; the first kind of ability is the brute ability to move matter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源意为「能够」；最基础的能力就是移动物体的蛮力。

senses.title: Control over people and decisions
senses.definition: the capacity to make others act or to determine collective decisions, whether through office, money or numbers
senses.definitionCN: 使他人行动或决定集体事务的能力，可来自职位、金钱或人数
senses.example: The union used its power to stop the layoffs.
senses.exampleCN: 工会动用它的力量阻止了裁员。
senses.why: Ability directed at people becomes influence; whoever can change what others do holds power.
senses.whyCN: 指向他人的能力变成影响力；能改变他人行为的人就握有权力。

senses.title: Capacity to produce an effect
senses.definition: the ability of a thing, substance or person to produce a particular effect
senses.definitionCN: 某物、某物质或某人产生特定效果的能力
senses.example: The drug has the power to relieve pain within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药能在几分钟内缓解疼痛。
senses.why: The same 'can' is at work here: the question is not who commands but what a thing is able to do.
senses.whyCN: 这里仍是同一个「能」：问题不是谁在下命令，而是某物能够做成什么。

senses.title: Electricity supplied to a place
senses.definition: electric energy supplied to homes, machines or a network
senses.definitionCN: 供给住宅、机器或电网的电能
senses.example: A fallen line cut the power to three streets before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前一条掉落的电线切断了三条街的供电。
senses.why: The industrial age narrowed the general word to the energy that makes machines able to work.
senses.whyCN: 工业时代把这一通用词收窄为让机器得以运转的能量。

senses.title: An exponent in mathematics
senses.definition: the number that shows how many times a base is multiplied by itself
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个底数被自身相乘多少次的数
senses.example: Two raised to the fifth power equals thirty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 二的五次方等于三十二。
senses.why: Repeated multiplication multiplies capacity, so mathematics named the count of multiplications by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 重复相乘使能力成倍增长，因此数学用同一个词来命名相乘的次数。

senses.title: Magnification of a lens
senses.definition: the factor by which an optical instrument enlarges a distant object
senses.definitionCN: 光学仪器把远处物体放大的倍数
senses.example: A ten-power lens brings the distant ridge into view.
senses.exampleCN: 十倍的镜头把远处的山脊拉到眼前。
senses.why: A lens multiplies the reach of the eye, so its factor is also called its power.
senses.whyCN: 镜头把眼睛的触及范围成倍扩大，因此它的倍数也被称为它的力量。

senses.title: A strong state on the world stage
senses.definition: a country able to influence other states through military, economic or diplomatic capacity
senses.definitionCN: 能通过军事、经济或外交能力影响他国的国家
senses.example: The two powers agreed to limit naval forces in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 两个强国同意限制该地区的海军力量。
senses.why: States are treated as single actors, so the ability to act becomes a nation's power.
senses.whyCN: 国家被当作单一行动者，因此行动的能力就成为一个国家的力量。

senses.title: Legal authority to act for another
senses.titleCN: 代他人行动的法定权限
senses.definition: a legal document or status allowing one person to act on another's behalf
senses.definitionCN: 允许一个人代另一人行动的法定文件或身份
senses.example: The daughter held power of attorney for her father.
senses.exampleCN: 女儿持有父亲的授权委托书。
senses.why: Law borrowed the word for a delegated ability: the agent can act because the principal's capacity has been transferred.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用这个词表示被授予的能力：代理人能行动，是因为本人的能力被转交了过来。

intro.en: Power came through Old French poeir from Vulgar Latin potere, from Latin posse 'to be able', built on potis 'able' and esse 'to be'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: power 经古法语 poeir 来自通俗拉丁 potere，再往上出自拉丁 posse「能够」，由 potis「有能力的」与 esse「是」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Potis meant 'able, capable, powerful'. Its pre-Latin origin is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: potis 意为「有能力的、能干的、有力量的」。它在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构，而非直接有据。

items.en: Potis plus esse produced posse, the verb 'to be able, can'.
items.cn: potis 加 esse 构成 posse，即动词「能够、可以」。

items.en: Everyday Latin reshaped the verb as potere, which became the ordinary verb for ability in the Romance languages.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁把这个动词改形为 potere，它后来成为罗曼语族中表示能力的常用动词。

items.en: Old French poeir carried both the verb and a noun for ability into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 poeir 在十三世纪把动词以及表示能力的名词一并带入英语。

items.en: Mathematics adopted the word for an exponent in the sixteenth century, and the electrical sense followed with the power grid in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 数学在十六世纪用这个词指幂指数；随着电网出现，电力义在十九世纪跟进。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of potis is a reconstruction, and no single first citation is fixed for the electrical sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：potis 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式；电力义也没有唯一的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same 'able' root; group two holds nouns for strength or influence seen from other angles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「能够」词根的词；第二组是从其他角度表示力量或影响力的名词。

entries.definition: Having great strength or influence; the adjective describes what the noun possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有强大力量或影响力的；形容词描述名词所拥有的东西。

entries.definition: Having no ability to act or change a situation; it is the direct negation of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 没有能力行动或改变处境的；是这个名词的直接否定。

entries.definition: Means strong in effect, especially of a drug or argument; it shares the Latin root of ability.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「效力强的」，尤指药物或论证；共享表示能力的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: An ability that exists but has not yet been exercised; it is power still folded up.
entries.definitionCN: 已存在但尚未施展的能力；是仍折叠未用的力量。

entries.definition: The physical quality of being strong; it covers muscles and materials rather than decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或结构上的强壮；覆盖肌肉与材料，而非决策。

entries.definition: Physical energy acting on an object, or organized pressure used to compel.
entries.definitionCN: 作用于物体的物理能量，或用来强迫的有组织压力。

entries.definition: Power that is recognized as rightful; power alone can be held without legitimacy.
entries.definitionCN: 被承认正当的权力；单纯的力量可以在缺乏正当性的情况下被持有。

entries.definition: The ability to change opinions or decisions without direct command.
entries.definitionCN: 不靠直接命令而改变意见或决定的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real 'able' root, the real derivatives and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「能够」词根、真实的派生词与真实的技术搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb means 'to be able'; every sense is a kind of ability, from moving a roof to lighting a street.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「能够」；每个义项都是一种能力，从掀翻屋顶到点亮街道。

normal.en: The family runs power, powerful, powerless, powerfully, powered, potent and potential.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 power、powerful、powerless、powerfully、powered、potent 与 potential。

normal.en: The political phrases are political power, balance of power and the powers.
normal.cn: 政治搭配有政治权力、力量均势与列强。

normal.en: The technical phrases are power supply, nuclear power and to the power of.
normal.cn: 技术搭配有电源、核能与……次方。

normal.en: The legal phrase is power of attorney, where one person acts for another.
normal.cn: 法律搭配是授权委托书，即一个人代另一个人行动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a master switch that lights a whole street at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在总闸上，一下点亮整条街。

abstract.en: Picture a number multiplied by itself again and again until it fills the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数反复自乘，直到写满整页。

abstract.en: Picture a signature that lets one person stand in another's shoes at a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名，让一个人在柜台前站进另一个人的位置。

examples.en: The engine's power is measured in kilowatts rather than horses.
examples.cn: 这台发动机的功率用千瓦而非马力来衡量。

examples.en: The committee has no power to change the budget on its own.
examples.cn: 委员会无权自行改变预算。

examples.en: Three to the fourth power is eighty-one.
examples.cn: 三的四次方是八十一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「能够」加「力」——能推动物体、能让人服从、能让灯亮 → 力量、权力、电力

root: power 经古法语来自通俗拉丁 potere，源头是拉丁 posse「能够」= potis「有能力的」+ esse「是」。potis 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one root idea, 'being able': able to move matter, able to command people, able to produce an effect, able to supply electricity, able to multiply a number, able to enlarge an image, able to act as a state, able to act for another person.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个词根观念「能够」展开：能移动物体、能命令他人、能产生效果、能供电、能使数字成倍、能放大图像、能作为国家行动、能代他人行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a master switch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在总闸上。

branches.en: THE BODY'S ABILITY: force that moves or breaks matter is the first meaning of being able.
branches.cn: 身体的能力：移动或破坏物体的力量，是「能够」的第一层含义。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL ABILITY: a union or a state acts because people and institutions can be made to move.
branches.cn: 社会的能力：工会或国家能行动，是因为可以使人及机构动起来。

branches.en: THE EFFECT: a drug or a word is powerful when it can change a body or a mind.
branches.cn: 效果：药物或言辞之所以有力，是因为它能改变身体或心智。

branches.en: THE CURRENT: the industrial age gave the general word to the energy that runs machines.
branches.cn: 电流：工业时代把这一通用词交给了驱动机器的能量。

branches.en: THE MEASURED AND DELEGATED: an exponent multiplies a number, a lens multiplies sight, and a legal document transfers capacity.
branches.cn: 可计量与可转交：指数使数字成倍，镜头使视力成倍，法律文件则转交能力。

intro.en: The word can be read from a Latin adjective of ability, the verb 'to be', the compound verb they form and the modern derived family.
intro.cn: 这个单词可以按表示能力的拉丁形容词、表示「是」的动词、由它们合成的动词以及现代派生词族逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin potis and esse give posse, the source of power; the same stem yields potent, potential and the noun potentia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 potis 与 esse 构成 posse，也就是 power 的来源；同一词干还衍生 potent、potential 与名词 potentia。

items.example: The adjective supplied the idea of capability.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「有能力」的观念。

items.example: The verb completes the compound meaning 'to be able'.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词补足「能够」的合成含义。

items.example: The Latin verb stated plain ability.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词表示单纯的能力。

items.example: The noun named capacity as a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指作为一种性质的能力。

items.example: The motor lost power on the climb.
items.exampleCN: 马达在爬坡时失去了动力。

items.example: A powerful storm crossed the coast.
The villagers felt powerless against the landslide.
items.exampleCN: 村民面对山体滑坡感到无能为力。

items.example: The speech argued powerfully for the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲为这座桥做了有力的论证。

items.example: The shed runs on solar-powered lights.
items.exampleCN: 棚屋使用太阳能驱动的灯。

items.example: The drug is potent at a very low dose.
items.exampleCN: 这种药在很低的剂量下就有效。

definition_zh: 强大的；有权势的；有影响力的；有力的；效力大的；感染力强的
definition_en: having great power, strength or influence, or able to produce a strong effect on people or things
core_image: 大坝深处一台水轮机被急流推动，钢铁外壳微微震动
scene: 山口的旧风车被换成了新的发电机，叶片在大风里转得飞快。The new turbine is powerful enough to light the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里 powerful 是「强大的、力量大的」（第 2 个义项：物理力量强）；句意为新水轮机的力量足以照亮整个村子。图中可辨识物件：山口、发电机、大风、叶片。

pos.zh: 强大的；有权势的；有力的；效力大的；感染力强的

senses.title: Having great power or influence
senses.definition: having a lot of control over people, events or decisions
senses.definitionCN: 对他人、事件或决定拥有很大的控制力
senses.example: The mayor is the most powerful figure in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 市长是这座城市里最有权势的人物。
senses.why: Power is the ability to make things happen, and -ful says a person is full of it; the first sense is power over other people.
senses.whyCN: power 是让事情发生的能力，-ful 表示「充满」，所以第一个义项是对他人的支配力。

senses.title: Physically strong or forceful
senses.definition: having great physical strength or able to produce a lot of force
senses.definitionCN: 具有很大的物理力量，或能产生很大的力
senses.example: The old truck has a surprisingly powerful engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧卡车的发动机力量大得惊人。
senses.why: The same fullness applies to machines and bodies, where power can be measured in force, speed or output rather than in votes.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「充满」也用在机器与身体上，那里的力量可以用力、速度或输出来衡量，而不是用选票。

senses.title: Producing a strong effect
senses.definition: having a strong effect on the body, on a situation or on a result
senses.definitionCN: 对身体、局势或结果产生强烈作用
senses.example: Doctors gave him a powerful drug for the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给他用了一种强效止痛药。
senses.why: If something acts with force on a body or on events, it is powerful in effect, so the word reaches medicine and argument as well as politics.
senses.whyCN: 某物若对身体或事态施加强力，就是在效果上强大，于是这个词也走进医药与论辩，不只属于政治。

senses.title: Moving or impressive
senses.titleCN: 感染力强的；令人震撼的
senses.definition: producing a strong emotional impression on an audience
senses.definitionCN: 在观众心里留下强烈的情感印象
senses.example: Her speech was powerful enough to silence the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的演讲感染力极强，整个礼堂都安静下来。
senses.why: An effect on feelings is still an effect; once the word measures impact, a film or a sentence can be powerful without any physical force.
senses.whyCN: 对情感的作用也是一种作用；一旦这个词开始衡量冲击力，一部电影或一句话即使没有物理力量也能是 powerful。

intro.en: Powerful is the noun power plus -ful, full of; power itself comes from Latin posse, to be able, through Old French.
intro.cn: powerful 是名词 power 加 -ful（充满）；power 本身经古法语上溯拉丁语 posse（能够）。

items.en: Posse meant to be able or to have the strength to do something, and it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: posse 意为能够、有力量做某事，是这一族词共同的根。

items.en: Everyday Latin used potere for can or be able, and this form spread through the provinces.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语用 potere 表示「能、可以」，这个形式在各省广泛流传。

items.en: Old French turned it into the noun poeir, meaning ability, strength or authority.
items.cn: 古法语把它变成名词 poeir，意为能力、力量或权威。

items.en: English borrowed power in the Middle Ages and added -ful to build an adjective meaning full of power.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪借入 power，并加上 -ful 造出表示「充满力量」的形容词。

items.en: Modern English applies powerful to people, states, engines, drugs, arguments and speeches, keeping one core of force.
items.cn: 现代英语把 powerful 用在人物、国家、发动机、药物、论据与演讲上，核心始终是「力量」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same power family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for strength and influence.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 power 词族的形式；近义组收表示力量与影响力的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun behind the adjective, naming ability, strength or control.
entries.definitionCN: 这一形容词背后的名词，指能力、力量或支配力。

entries.definition: In a powerful way, with great force or effect.
entries.definitionCN: 由 powerful 加 -ly 构成，义为「强有力地」。

entries.definition: Without power or the ability to act.
entries.definitionCN: 由 power 加 -less 构成，义为「无力的；无能为力的」。

entries.definition: A power station, or a person or group full of energy and strength.
entries.definitionCN: 由 power 与 house 复合，指发电厂，也指精力充沛的人或机构。

entries.definition: Having great physical strength, often in the body or in a material.
entries.definitionCN: 强壮的；多指身体或材料本身的强度。

entries.definition: Very strong or great, a word with an old and slightly literary ring.
entries.definitionCN: 强大的；气势宏大的，带古老且偏文学的色彩。

entries.definition: Full of force in expression or action, often said of people and words.
entries.definitionCN: 有力的；多形容表达或行动，常指人与言辞。

entries.definition: Able to change decisions or opinions indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 有影响力的；强调间接改变决定或看法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a noun of ability with a suffix meaning full of, and its family keeps returning to force, control and effect.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示能力的名词加上「充满」的后缀，同族词反复回到力量、支配与效果。

normal.en: Power comes from Latin posse, to be able, through Old French poeir.
normal.cn: power 来自拉丁语 posse（能够），经古法语 poeir 传入。

normal.en: -ful means full of, so powerful is simply full of power, with no other root involved.
normal.cn: -ful 意为「充满」，所以 powerful 就是「充满力量」，没有别的词根。

normal.en: Powerless swaps -ful for -less and turns the meaning around.
normal.cn: powerless 把 -ful 换成 -less，意思就反了过来。

normal.en: A powerful engine and a powerful argument share one idea: both move something with force.
normal.cn: 力量大的发动机与有力的论据共用一个想法：都以力推动某物。

normal.en: Powerfully adds -ly and describes how that force is applied.
normal.cn: powerfully 加 -ly，描述这股力量是怎样施加的。

abstract.en: Power is the ability to make something happen, and powerful measures how much of that ability a thing holds.
abstract.cn: 力量是让事情发生的能力，powerful 衡量的就是某物握有多少这种能力。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a person to a machine because both can push the world in a chosen direction.
abstract.cn: 这个词能轻易从人转到机器，因为两者都能把世界推向某个选定的方向。

abstract.en: A powerful speech leaves the room different, which shows that force is not only physical.
abstract.cn: 一场感染力强的演讲会让房间变得不同，可见力量并不只属于身体。

examples.en: The new turbine is powerful enough to light the whole village.
examples.cn: 新水轮机的力量足以照亮整个村子。

examples.en: The mayor is the most powerful figure in the city.
examples.cn: 市长是这座城市里最有权势的人物。

examples.en: Doctors gave him a powerful drug for the pain.
examples.cn: 医生给他用了一种强效止痛药。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「炮火」——炮火一响，声势逼人；powerful 就是强大的、有力的。

root: 由名词 power 加形容词后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成；power 经古法语 poeir 上溯通俗拉丁语 potere 与拉丁语 posse（能够），与 potent、potential 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being full of power; the senses divide into social influence, physical force, strong effect and emotional impact.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「充满力量」；义项由此分出社会权势、物理力量、强烈效力与情感冲击。

core.cn: 核心意象：大坝深处一台水轮机被急流推动，钢铁外壳微微震动。

branches.cn: 市长走向一排麦克风

branches.en: a turbine turning under rushing water
branches.cn: 水轮机在水流下转动

branches.en: a small vial of a drug that stops the pain
branches.cn: 一小瓶止住疼痛的药

branches.cn: 一句话之后整个礼堂安静下来

branches.cn: 一台力量足以吊起满载卡车的机器

intro.en: The adjective is the noun power plus a suffix meaning full of, and the noun itself goes back to a Latin verb for being able.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是名词 power 加上表示「充满」的后缀，而名词本身上溯一个意为「能够」的拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: Powerful rests on Latin posse, to be able, and its everyday form potere, which Old French turned into the noun poeir; potent and potential share the same root.
latinIntro.cn: powerful 立足于拉丁语 posse（能够）及其日常形式 potere，古法语由此造出名词 poeir；potent 与 potential 同出一根。

items.meaning: to be able, to have power

definition_zh: 实际的；实践的；实用的；可行的；注重实际的；务实的
definition_en: relating to real actions and situations rather than ideas, useful for a real purpose, likely to work, or sensible about everyday needs
core_image: 一张折起的图纸被塞进工具袋，袋口露出半截卷尺
scene: 教室后面的工作台上，几个学生把图纸放下，开始用木条搭架子。The course gives students practical experience with real tools.
sceneCN: 这里 practical 是「实际的、实践的」（第 1 个义项：与真实行动有关，而非只讲理论）；句意为这门课让学生在真实工具上获得实际经验。图中可辨识物件：工作台、图纸、木条、工具袋。

pos.zh: 实际的；实践的；实用的；可行的；注重实际的；务实的

collocations.zh: 实际上；就实际效果而言

derivatives.zh: 由 practical 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上；几乎」
由 practical 加 -ity 构成，义为「实用性；可行性」

senses.title: Concerned with action rather than theory
senses.definition: connected with real actions and situations rather than with ideas or rules alone
senses.definitionCN: 与真实行动和情形相连，而不只是与观念或规则相连
senses.example: Students need practical experience before they apply for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在申请这份工作之前需要有实际经验。
senses.why: Greek praktikos meant fit for action, so the adjective begins by pointing at doing rather than at thinking; the first sense keeps that contrast alive.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 praktikos 意为「适合行动的」，所以这个形容词从一开始就指向做而不是想；第一个义项保留的正是这组对照。

senses.title: Useful for a real purpose
senses.definition: designed to be useful in real use rather than attractive or clever
senses.definitionCN: 为真实使用而设计得有用，而不是为了好看或机巧
senses.example: The kit contains a practical set of tools for small repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这套工具里是一组做小修小补很实用的工具。
senses.why: If a thing suits action, it is useful, and the word passes from the situation to the object that fits it.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西若适合行动，就是有用的；词义于是从情形转到适合这个情形的物件上。

senses.title: Likely to work
senses.definition: possible to carry out and likely to succeed in real conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在真实条件下做得到、并且很可能成功
senses.example: Building a footbridge here is the most practical solution.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里修一座人行桥是最可行的办法。
senses.why: A plan is practical when it survives real conditions, so the adjective shifts from describing tools to judging proposals.
senses.whyCN: 一个方案能在真实条件下站住，就是可行的；形容词于是从评价器物转向评判方案。

senses.title: Sensible about everyday needs
senses.definition: of a person, dealing with things as they are and not chasing impractical ideas
senses.definitionCN: 指人按事物的实际情况办事，不追求不切实际的想法
senses.example: She is practical about money and never buys on impulse.
senses.exampleCN: 她花钱很务实，从不冲动购物。
senses.why: A person whose habits suit action is called practical, which is how the word reaches character and not just objects.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的习惯若总适合行动，就会被称作务实；这个词由此触及性格，而不只是器物。

intro.en: Practical follows an action word from Greek through Latin and French: praktikos, practicus, pratique, and finally the English adjective built on practice.
intro.cn: practical 沿着一个表示行动的词从希腊语经拉丁语与法语走来：praktikos、practicus、pratique，最后是英语在 practice 上造出的形容词。

items.en: The Greek verb prassein meant to do, to act or to carry something through.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 prassein 意为做、行动或把事情办成。

items.en: Praktikos was formed from it to mean fit for action, practical rather than theoretical.
items.cn: 由它构成的 praktikos 意为「适合行动的」，指务实的而非理论的。

items.en: Latin took the adjective as practicus, used for what concerns action or practice.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个形容词借作 practicus，用于表示与行动或实践有关的事物。

items.en: English borrowed practice through Old French, first for the doing of something and then for repeated exercise.
items.cn: 英语经古法语借入 practice，先指做某件事，后指反复练习。

items.en: Modern English built practical on practice with -al, and the word spread to tools, plans, people and purposes.
items.cn: 现代英语在 practice 上加 -al 造出 practical，这个词随后扩展到工具、方案、人与目的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same practice family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what works in real conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 practice 词族的形式；近义组收形容在真实条件下行得通的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for doing something repeatedly or for the usual way of doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，指反复练习，或通常的做法。

entries.definition: In a practical way, and in everyday use also almost.
entries.definitionCN: 由 practical 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上」，日常也指「几乎」。

entries.definition: The quality of being useful or workable.
entries.definitionCN: 由 practical 加 -ity 构成，义为「实用性；可行性」。

entries.definition: Not sensible or not possible to carry out.
entries.definitionCN: 由否定前缀 im- 加 practical 构成，义为「不切实际的」。

entries.definition: Dealing with things according to what works rather than what is ideal.
entries.definitionCN: 务实的；按是否行得通而非是否理想来处理事情。

entries.definition: Accepting the facts of a situation and not expecting too much.
entries.definitionCN: 现实的；接受实际情况，不抱过高期望。

entries.definition: Able to help you do something or get what you want.
entries.definitionCN: 有用的；能帮人做成事或得到想要的东西。

entries.definition: Able to be used or carried out successfully.
entries.definitionCN: 可行的；能够实施并取得效果的。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Greek verb for doing, and its family keeps returning to action, use and what actually works.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自希腊语表示「做」的动词，同族词反复回到行动、用途以及真正行得通的东西。

normal.en: Practical goes back through Latin practicus to Greek praktikos, fit for action.
normal.cn: practical 经拉丁语 practicus 上溯希腊语 praktikos（适合行动的）。

normal.en: The Greek verb prassein means to do, so the word is about doing rather than about thinking.
normal.cn: 希腊语动词 prassein 意为做，所以这个词讲的是做，而不是想。

normal.en: Practice is the noun for doing something repeatedly, and practical describes what suits that doing.
normal.cn: practice 是表示反复做某事的名词，practical 则形容适合这种做的东西。

normal.en: Impractical adds im- and names what cannot be carried out in real conditions.
normal.cn: impractical 加 im-，指在真实条件下办不成的事。

normal.en: Practically is the adverb of the same family, and it also picked up the everyday sense of almost.
normal.cn: practically 是同族的副词，还另外长出了「几乎」这个日常义。

abstract.en: A practical idea is one that survives contact with a real room, a real budget and a real deadline.
abstract.cn: 一个实用的想法，是能挺过真实房间、真实预算与真实期限的想法。

abstract.en: Theory describes what should happen; the practical answer is what still works when it does not.
abstract.cn: 理论描述本该发生什么；可行的答案则在事情没按预期发生时仍然管用。

abstract.en: Calling a person practical is a quiet compliment: it means the world rarely surprises them.
abstract.cn: 说一个人务实是含蓄的称赞：意思是世界很少让他措手不及。

examples.en: The course gives students practical experience with real tools.
examples.cn: 这门课让学生用真实工具获得实际经验。

examples.en: Building a footbridge here is the most practical solution.
examples.cn: 在这里修一座人行桥是最可行的办法。

examples.en: She is practical about money and never buys on impulse.
examples.cn: 她花钱很务实，从不冲动购物。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「适合行动」；义项由此分出真实经验、实用、可行性，以及务实的性情。

intro.en: Greek action words passed through Latin and French, and English built the adjective on practice with the suffix -al.
intro.cn: 表示行动的希腊词经拉丁语与法语传来，英语又在 practice 上加 -al 造出这个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Practical reaches back to Greek praxis and praktikos, which Latin took as practicus; the English adjective itself was formed later on practice.
latinIntro.cn: practical 上溯希腊语 praxis 与 praktikos，拉丁语借作 practicus；英语形容词本身则是后来在 practice 上造出的。

definition_zh: 几乎；差不多；实际上；在实践中；以实用的方式；从实际出发
definition_en: almost or very nearly, in real conditions rather than in theory, or in a way that deals with real needs
core_image: 一只杯子立在桌边，水面几乎碰到杯口，只差一线就溢出
scene: 暴雨后的巷子里，积水已经漫到台阶最上一级。By evening the road was practically a river.
sceneCN: 这里 practically 是「几乎、差不多」（第 1 个义项：非常接近但还不是）；句意为到了傍晚，这条路几乎成了一条河。图中可辨识物件：巷子、积水、台阶。

pos.zh: 几乎；差不多；实际上；在实践中；以实用的方式

derivatives.zh: 由 practically 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「实际的；实用的」
由 practical 加 -ity 构成，义为「实用性；可行性」
由否定前缀 im- 加 practical 构成，义为「不切实际的；不可行的」

senses.title: Almost, very nearly
senses.definition: almost, so close to something that the difference hardly matters
senses.definitionCN: 几乎，接近到差别几乎无关紧要的程度
senses.example: It is practically impossible to finish the report tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚要写完这份报告几乎不可能。
senses.why: The sense grows out of the older meaning in effect: if something is true for every practical purpose, speakers slide from in effect to almost.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从较早的「在效果上」长出来：若一件事在所有实际用途上都成立，说话人便从「在效果上」滑到「几乎」。

senses.title: In real conditions rather than in theory
senses.definition: when real conditions are considered rather than the theory behind them
senses.definitionCN: 考虑真实条件，而不是背后的理论
senses.example: Practically speaking, the plan costs more than we can afford.
senses.exampleCN: 实际上，这个计划的费用超出我们的承受能力。
senses.why: The adverb is simply practical plus -ly, so it names the way things stand once an idea meets a real budget or a real room.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词就是 practical 加 -ly，指的就是一个想法碰上真实预算或真实房间之后的情形。

senses.title: In a practical way
senses.titleCN: 以实用的方式；从实际出发
senses.definition: by dealing with real things and real limits instead of following an abstract method
senses.definitionCN: 按真实的事物与限制来办事，而不照着抽象的方法做
senses.example: She fixed the pump practically, with a torch and a short list of steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手电筒和几行步骤，按实际可行的办法修好了水泵。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the plain -ly adverb of practical describes the manner of action, before the word ever came to mean almost.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：practical 加 -ly 的副词本义描述做事的方式，早于它表示「几乎」。

intro.en: Practically is practical plus -ly, and both go back to a Greek verb for doing; the everyday sense almost is a later extension of in effect.
intro.cn: practically 是 practical 加 -ly，两者都上溯一个表示「做」的希腊动词；日常的「几乎」义是「在效果上」的后来引申。

items.en: The Greek verb prassein meant to do or to act, and praxis was the noun for action.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 prassein 意为做、行动，名词 praxis 指行动。

items.en: Praktikos meant fit for action and described what serves doing rather than theorising.
items.cn: praktikos 意为适合行动的，用来形容服务于做而非空谈的东西。

items.en: Latin adopted the adjective as practicus, and its adverb practice carried the same sense of action.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个形容词借作 practicus，相应的副词同样带着「行动」的含义。

items.en: English formed practical from practice with -al, then added -ly to make the adverb in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语在 practice 上加 -al 造出 practical，十六、十七世纪又加 -ly 造出副词。

items.en: Modern English extended the adverb to mean almost, and phrases such as practically speaking keep both the old and the new senses in view.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词扩展到「几乎」，而 practically speaking 一类说法同时保留了旧义与新义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same practice family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of near-completeness and effect.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 practice 词族的形式；近义组收表示接近完成与效果实际的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb, meaning useful or suited to action.
entries.definitionCN: 这一副词背后的形容词，义为实用的、适合行动的。

entries.definition: The noun for doing something repeatedly or in the usual way.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，指反复做或通常的做法。

entries.definition: The quality of being useful or possible to carry out.
entries.definitionCN: 由 practical 加 -ity 构成，义为「实用性；可行性」。

entries.definition: Not sensible or not possible in real conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 由否定前缀 im- 加 practical 构成，义为「不切实际的」。

entries.definition: Not quite, but very close to a state or an amount.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎；非常接近某种状态或数量，但还不是。

entries.definition: In effect, though not in a strict or formal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上；就效果而言，而非严格或正式意义上。

entries.definition: A little less than, or a little before, something.
entries.definitionCN: 将近；比某数量略少，或比某时点略早。

entries.definition: In effect, even if not officially or literally.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上；即便不是名义上或字面上如此。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adverb of practical, and its family keeps returning to action, while the sense almost grows out of in effect.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 practical 的副词，同族词反复回到行动，而「几乎」义则从「在效果上」长出。

normal.en: Practically is practical plus -ly, so its base meaning is in a practical way.
normal.cn: practically 是 practical 加 -ly，所以本义是「以实际的方式」。

normal.en: The adverb later drifted to almost: what is practically true is true for all useful purposes.
normal.cn: 这个副词后来漂到「几乎」：在实际上成立的事，对所有实际用途都成立。

normal.en: Practicality is the noun of the same family, naming the quality of being workable.
normal.cn: practicality 是同族的名词，指可行性这种性质。

normal.en: Impractical adds im- to practical and means not workable in real conditions.
normal.cn: impractical 在 practical 前加 im-，指在真实条件下行不通。

normal.en: Practically speaking is a fixed phrase that announces a judgement about real conditions.
normal.cn: practically speaking 是固定说法，用来引出对真实条件的判断。

abstract.en: Practically sits between yes and no: it says the difference is real but too small to matter.
abstract.cn: practically 站在「是」与「否」之间：它说差别确实存在，却小到无关紧要。

abstract.en: A road that is practically a river is not a river, yet no car will pass.
abstract.cn: 一条几乎成了河的路并不是河，但没有车能过去。

abstract.en: The word measures the gap between the rule and the world, then decides the gap can be ignored.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量规则与世界之间的差距，然后判定这道差距可以忽略。

examples.en: By evening the road was practically a river.
examples.cn: 到了傍晚，这条路几乎成了一条河。

examples.en: It is practically impossible to finish the report tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚要写完这份报告几乎不可能。

examples.en: Practically speaking, the plan costs more than we can afford.
examples.cn: 实际上，这个计划的费用超出我们的承受能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来克提扣里」——扣得上的东西几乎都合用；practically 就是几乎、实际上。

root: 由 practical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；词干可上溯希腊语 prassein（做、行动）与 praktikos（适合行动的），经拉丁语 practicus 与古法语 pratique 传入英语。表示「几乎」的义项一般认为从「在实际效果上」的用法引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what holds in practice; the senses divide into the manner of acting, the reality of a situation, and the everyday drift to almost.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「在实践中成立」；义项由此分出做事的做法、局面的实情，以及日常用法里向「几乎」的漂移。

intro.en: The adverb is practical plus -ly, and the whole family goes back to a Greek verb meaning to do.
intro.cn: 这个副词是 practical 加 -ly，整族词都上溯一个意为「做」的希腊动词。

latinIntro.en: Practically inherits the Latin adjective practicus and the English practical; the Latin line itself goes back to Greek praktikos, fit for action.

definition_zh: 练习；实践；惯例；诊所；执业

senses.title: Repeated exercise to improve a skill
senses.definition: the repeated doing of an activity in order to become better at it
senses.definitionCN: 为了变得更熟练而反复进行某项活动
senses.example: Daily practice is the only way to play that passage smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 每日练习是把这个乐段弹流畅的唯一办法。
senses.why: The Greek root meant doing rather than knowing, so practice begins as action repeated until the body remembers it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根强调的是一遍遍去做，而不是想明白，所以 practice 的起点是反复行动，直到身体自己记住。

senses.title: The actual doing of an idea
senses.definition: the carrying out of a plan, belief or method in real situations rather than only talking about it
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、信念或方法放到真实情境中实行，而不只是谈论
senses.example: The new rules look fair on paper but are hard in practice.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定在纸面上看着公平，实践起来却很难。
senses.why: If the core is repeated action, the same noun can name the moment an idea leaves the page and turns into something done.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心是反复的行动，这个名词也就能指想法离开纸面、变成实际行动的那一刻。

senses.title: A usual way of doing things
senses.definition: a habit or accepted custom, especially one followed by a group or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 习惯或被普遍接受的做法，尤指某一群体或行业沿用的方式
senses.example: It is common practice to confirm a booking by email.
senses.exampleCN: 用电子邮件确认预订是常见的做法。
senses.why: What is done again and again hardens into a rule, so practice slides from one person's repetition to a group's settled custom.
senses.whyCN: 反复去做的事会慢慢固化成规矩，于是 practice 从一个人的重复，滑向一群人的既定惯例。

senses.title: The business of a professional
senses.definition: the work of a doctor or lawyer, and the place where that work is done
senses.definitionCN: 医生或律师所从事的工作，以及开展这项工作的场所
senses.example: She runs a small practice in the town centre.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市中心经营一家小诊所。
senses.why: A profession rests on practised skill, so the word comes to name the professional's ongoing work and the rooms where it happens.
senses.whyCN: 一门职业建立在反复练就的本领之上，所以这个词又用来指专业人士长期从事的业务，以及开展业务的场所。

intro.en: Practice travels through Latin and French back to a Greek word for doing, and its modern spelling split belongs to English alone.
intro.cn: practice 经拉丁语和法语上溯到希腊语中表示「做」的词，而它现代拼写的分工是英语自己后来形成的。

items.en: The verb prassein, in its Attic form prattein, meant to do, to act or to achieve, and it is the earliest recoverable source of the family.
items.cn: 动词 prassein（阿提卡方言作 prattein）意为做、行动、完成，是这一族词最早可追溯的来源。

items.en: The adjective praktikos described a person or thing fit for action, as opposed to merely theoretical.
items.cn: 形容词 praktikos 形容适合行动的、能实干的，与只停留在理论上的东西相对。

items.en: Latin took praktikos as practicus, and medieval Latin formed the noun practica for practical knowledge or the actual doing of something.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 praktikos 借作 practicus，中世纪拉丁语又造出名词 practica，指实用知识或实际去做。

items.en: Old French practique and the verb practiser carried the words into daily use, and English borrowed both in the centuries after the Norman settlement.
items.cn: 古法语 practique 与动词 practiser 把这些词带入日常使用，英语在诺曼人定居后的几个世纪里把两者都借了进来。

items.en: British English keeps practice for the noun and practise for the verb, while American English uses practice for both; the -ice and -ise endings are the everyday marker of that division.
items.cn: 英式英语用 practice 作名词、practise 作动词，美式英语则名词动词都写 practice；-ice 与 -ise 两种词尾就是这一分工的日常标记。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the spelling pair and the Latin-derived family; the near-meaning group gathers words for training, habit and real application.
note.cn: 形近组收这一对拼写以及拉丁来源的词族；近义组收表示训练、习惯与真正实行的词。

entries.definition: The British verb form, used for doing an activity repeatedly or working in a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 英式动词拼写，表示反复做某事或在某一行业执业。

entries.definition: Concerned with real action rather than with theory.
entries.definitionCN: 关乎实际行动而非理论的；实用的。

entries.definition: A person who works in a profession such as medicine or law.
entries.definitionCN: 从事医学、法律等职业的人；从业者。

entries.definition: A course of supervised practical work for students.
entries.definitionCN: 学生在督导下进行的实习课程。

entries.definition: Activity done repeatedly to train the body or the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 为训练身体或头脑而反复进行的活动。

entries.definition: A run-through of a performance before the real one.
entries.definitionCN: 正式演出之前的排练。

entries.definition: Something a person does regularly, often without thinking about it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人经常做、往往不假思索的事。

entries.definition: An accepted way of behaving in a group or a society.
entries.definitionCN: 群体或社会中已被接受的行为方式。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by a Greek verb for doing, a Latin adjective for fitness to act, and an English split between the noun and the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「做」的希腊动词、表示「适于行动」的拉丁形容词，以及英语里名词与动词的拼写分工共同支撑。

normal.en: Greek prattein means to do, so practice is tied to action from the start rather than to theory.
normal.cn: 希腊语 prattein 意为做，所以 practice 从一开始就绑在行动上，而不是理论上。

normal.en: Latin practicus meant fit for action, and English practical keeps that sense of something usable rather than abstract.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 practicus 意为适于行动的，英语 practical 保留了「能用得上」而不是「抽象」的意味。

normal.en: British English marks the job with -ise: practise is the verb and practice is the noun.
normal.cn: 英式英语用 -ise 标出动词身份：practise 是动词，practice 是名词。

normal.en: American English drops the distinction and writes practice for both, which is why a spell-checker may object to practise.
normal.cn: 美式英语不分名词动词，一律写 practice，所以拼写检查常常会对 practise 提出异议。

normal.en: Practitioner adds a person suffix to the same stem and names someone who practises a profession.
normal.cn: practitioner 在同一词干后加上表示人的后缀，指从事某一职业的人。

abstract.en: Picture a pianist's fingers finding the keys without the eyes: practice is memory stored in the body.
abstract.cn: 想象钢琴家的手指不看琴键也能落准：practice 就是存进身体里的记忆。

abstract.en: A plan on paper becomes practice the moment someone follows it out in the rain.
abstract.cn: 纸上的计划，在有人冒着雨照着去做的那一刻才成为 practice。

abstract.en: A clinic is called a practice because a doctor's skill stays alive through seeing patients, not through holding a certificate.
abstract.cn: 诊所之所以叫 practice，是因为医生的本领靠一次次接诊维持，而不是靠一张证书。

examples.en: Her daily practice on the piano lasts forty minutes.
examples.cn: 她每天在钢琴上练习四十分钟。

examples.en: The rule works well in practice.
examples.cn: 这条规则在实践中效果很好。

examples.en: He joined a small legal practice after graduating.
examples.cn: 毕业后他加入了一家小型律师事务所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来个题」——考前扑来一堆题，正好拿来练手；记住 practice 是练习。

root: 希腊语 prassein/prattein（做、行动）→ 形容词 praktikos（适于行动的）→ 拉丁语 practicus 与中世纪拉丁语名词 practica（实用知识、实行）→ 古法语 practique/practiser → 英语 practice/practise。英式分工为名词 practice、动词 practise，美式为两者皆写 practice。

sensesIntro.en: The core is repeated action; from it come the doing of an idea, the custom that repetition creates, and the professional work built on practised skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是反复的行动；由此长出把想法付诸实行、重复所养成的惯例，以及建立在熟练本领之上的专业执业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same scale played again and again until the fingers remember it.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一段音阶被反复弹奏，直到手指自己记住。

branches.en: a metronome ticking beside a closed piano lid
branches.cn: 合上的琴盖旁，节拍器还在响

branches.en: a printed rule stepped on by wet boots
branches.cn: 印着规则的纸被湿靴子踩过

branches.en: the same greeting repeated at every shop door
branches.cn: 每家店门口重复的同一句招呼

branches.en: a waiting room with three chairs and a name plate
branches.cn: 摆着三把椅子和一块名牌的候诊室

branches.en: skill kept alive by daily repetition and daily clients
branches.cn: 靠每日重复与每日病患维持的本领

intro.en: A Greek verb of doing, a Latin adjective of practical fitness and two rival English endings carry the whole word.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的希腊动词、一个表示「适于实干」的拉丁形容词，加上两种相互竞争的英语词尾，撑起了整个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin and medieval Latin layers are well recorded and supply both the adjective and the noun behind this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语与中世纪拉丁语这两层有清楚记录，为这个词提供了形容词与名词两个来源。

items.meaning: to do repeatedly, to work in a profession

items.meaningCN: 名词词尾：状态、性质、事物

definition_zh: 练习；执业；奉行；施展（手法）
definition_en: the British spelling of the verb meaning to do something repeatedly in order to improve, to work as a doctor or lawyer, to follow a religion or custom, or to perform a trick
core_image: 一个人对着镜子把同一句台词念到嘴唇自己会动，镜面上全是呼出的白雾
scene: 剧场后台只剩一盏化妆灯，演员对着镜子把同一句台词又念了一遍，声音沙哑却没有停。She practises the line until it sounds like a thought rather than a recitation.
sceneCN: 这里 practise 是「练习」（第 1 个义项：为熟练而反复做某事）；句意为她反复练那句台词，直到它听起来像临时想到的，而不是背出来的。画面里有化妆灯、镜子和沙哑的嗓音。

pos.zh: 练习；执业；奉行；施展（手法）

derivatives.zh: 由 practise 的过去分词转作形容词，义为「熟练的；老练的」
由 practise 的现在分词转作形容词，义为「执业中的；正在从事某职业的」
英式英语中与动词 practise 分工的名词形式，义为「练习；实践；诊所」
由 practise 的词干加表示从业者的后缀构成，义为「从业者」

senses.title: To do something repeatedly in order to improve
senses.definition: to do an activity many times so that your skill at it improves
senses.definitionCN: 反复进行某项活动，使自己的技能有所提高
senses.example: She practises the violin for an hour before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她早饭前练一个小时小提琴。
senses.why: The Greek source meant to do, so the verb starts from the plain act of doing a thing over and over rather than from thinking about it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为「做」，所以这个动词的起点就是把一件事一遍遍做下去，而不是在脑子里琢磨。

senses.title: To work in a profession
senses.definition: to work as a doctor, lawyer or other trained professional
senses.definitionCN: 以医生、律师或其他受过训练的专业人士身份工作
senses.example: He has practised law in this city for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这个城市当了二十年律师。
senses.why: Professional work is skill applied daily, so the verb that means repeating an action also names the lifelong carrying out of a trained job.
senses.whyCN: 专业工作就是每天把本领用出来，所以表示反复练习的动词，也用来指把受训得来的职业做一辈子。

senses.title: To follow a religion or custom
senses.definition: to observe the rules and ceremonies of a religion or a traditional custom
senses.definitionCN: 遵守某种宗教或传统习俗的规矩与仪式
senses.example: Her family still practises the old harvest festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她家仍然遵行古老的丰收节习俗。
senses.why: A custom survives only by being done again each year, and the verb for repeated doing fits that annual repetition exactly.
senses.whyCN: 习俗只有年年重新做一遍才能延续，而表示反复去做的动词，正好贴合这种一年一度的重复。

senses.title: To carry out a trick or method
senses.definition: to perform a trick or use a method, especially one that is repeated on new victims
senses.definitionCN: 施展某种手法或使用某种办法，尤指把同一套把戏用在新的对象身上
senses.example: The swindler practised the same trick on three families.
senses.exampleCN: 那个骗子把同一套把戏用在了三户人家身上。
senses.why: If the core is doing something again and again, the word can also describe a trick worked repeatedly on whoever comes next.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心是一遍遍去做，这个词也就能描述一套把戏，反复用在下一个上钩的人身上。

intro.en: Practise shares its whole history with practice, but English sends the verb down the -ise path and keeps -ice for the noun.
intro.cn: practise 与 practice 共享全部历史，只是英语让动词走 -ise 一路，把 -ice 留给名词。

items.en: The verb prassein, Attic prattein, meant to do or to achieve, and the whole family grows from the idea of action.
items.cn: 动词 prassein（阿提卡方言 prattein）意为做、完成，整个词族都从这个「行动」的念头长出来。

items.en: Praktikos described what is fit for action, a word about real work rather than abstract knowledge.
items.cn: praktikos 形容适合行动的，说的是实际动手，而不是抽象知识。

items.en: Latin practicus and the medieval verb practicare named practical action, and the noun practica named the knowledge gained by doing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 practicus 与中世纪动词 practicare 指实际去做，名词 practica 则指通过实践得来的知识。

items.en: Old French practiser, also written pratiquer, meant to put into practice or to carry on a profession, and English took the verb form from it.
items.cn: 古法语 practiser（也写作 pratiquer）意为付诸实践或从事某职业，英语的动词形式就是从它借来的。

items.en: Middle English practisen settled into practise, and British English now keeps practise for the verb while American English uses practice for both; the split is a spelling convention, not a difference in meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语 practisen 定型为 practise，如今英式英语用 practise 作动词、practice 作名词，美式英语两者都写 practice；这一分工只是拼写惯例，并不带来含义差别。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun twin and the Latin-derived family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for training, drilling and carrying something out.
note.cn: 形近组收与它配对的名词形式以及拉丁来源的词族；近义组收表示训练、操练与执行的动词。

entries.definition: The noun in British English, and both noun and verb in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中的名词，在美式英语中则名词动词同形。

entries.definition: Useful and concerned with real action rather than theory.
entries.definitionCN: 有用的、关乎实际行动而非理论的。

entries.definition: A person who practises a profession such as medicine or law.
entries.definitionCN: 从事医学、法律等职业的从业者。

entries.definition: A period of supervised practical training for students.
entries.definitionCN: 学生接受督导的实践训练期。

entries.definition: To practise a performance before showing it to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前演出之前进行排练。

entries.definition: To teach and exercise someone over time for a skill or a job.
entries.definitionCN: 用一段时间教导并训练某人掌握技能或胜任工作。

entries.definition: To make someone repeat an exercise until it becomes automatic.
entries.definitionCN: 让人反复做同一练习直到变成自动反应。

entries.definition: To perform a plan, order or method in real life.
entries.definitionCN: 在现实中执行计划、命令或方法。

normalIntro.en: The verb keeps the Greek sense of doing, the Latin layer of practical action, and a British spelling rule that separates it from the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词保留了希腊语「做」的意思与拉丁语「实际行动」这一层，再加一条把它跟名词分开的英式拼写规则。

normal.en: Practise uses -ise because British English marks verbs with that ending, as in realise and organise.
normal.cn: practise 用 -ise，是因为英式英语用这个词尾标记动词，就像 realise 与 organise。

normal.en: Practice uses -ice because it is the noun, just as advice is the noun beside the verb advise.
normal.cn: practice 用 -ice，因为它是名词，就像 advice 是名词、advise 是动词一样。

normal.en: American English uses practice for the verb too, so only British texts insist on the s.
normal.cn: 美式英语的动词也写 practice，所以只有英式文本才坚持用 s。

normal.en: The -ed form practised keeps the s and doubles nothing: practise, practised, practising.
normal.cn: 加 -ed 的过去式 practised 保留 s，也不双写任何字母：practise、practised、practising。

normal.en: Practise what you preach is the idiom that shows the plainest sense: do the thing, do not just talk about it.
normal.cn: practise what you preach 这个说法体现了最朴素的一层：真去做，而不只是嘴上讲。

abstract.en: A mirror in a cold dressing room is where skill is built: the same line, the same breath, again.
abstract.cn: 冷清的化妆间里那面镜子，就是本领被磨出来的地方：同一句词、同一口气，再来一遍。

abstract.en: A licence on the wall means nothing until the lawyer practises daily in front of real clients.
abstract.cn: 墙上的执照本身不算什么，直到律师每天在真实的当事人面前执业。

abstract.en: A custom lives only while someone practises it, which is why the verb also means to keep a tradition going.
abstract.cn: 习俗只有在有人继续照做时才活着，所以这个动词也意味着把传统延续下去。

examples.en: She practises the violin for an hour before breakfast.
examples.cn: 她早饭前练一个小时小提琴。

examples.en: He has practised law in this city for twenty years.
examples.cn: 他在这个城市当了二十年律师。

examples.en: The swindler practised the same trick on three families.
examples.cn: 那个骗子把同一套把戏用在了三户人家身上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来个试」——一个接一个的试验扑过来，练的就是手上功夫；记住 practise 是练习。

root: 与 practice 同源：希腊语 prassein/prattein（做）→ praktikos（适于行动的）→ 拉丁语 practicus → 中世纪拉丁语 practica/practicare → 古法语 practiser → 中古英语 practisen。英式英语中动词固定写作 practise、名词写作 practice；美式英语动词与名词都写 practice。

sensesIntro.en: The core is doing a thing over and over; the senses run from training a skill, to living by a profession, to keeping a custom, to working a trick on new victims.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把一件事反复做下去；义项从磨练技能，延伸到以某职业为生、遵行某种习俗，再到把一套把戏用在新的对象身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a performer repeating one line at a mirror until the words come without effort.
core.cn: 核心意象：演员对着镜子重复同一句台词，直到字句毫不费力地出来。

branches.en: a mirror, a lamp and one line said thirty times
branches.cn: 一面镜子、一盏灯和一句念了三十遍的台词

branches.en: a brass plate on a solicitor's door
branches.cn: 律师门上一块黄铜名牌

branches.en: a family bowing at the same hour each week
branches.cn: 一家人每周同一时刻躬身

branches.en: the same trick played on a third stranger
branches.cn: 同一个把戏用在第三个陌生人身上

branches.en: hours of drill turning into a licence to work
branches.cn: 长时间操练换来一张执业许可

intro.en: A Greek verb of doing, a Latin verb of practical action, and the English verb ending -ise hold this spelling together.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的希腊动词、一个表示实际施行的拉丁动词，以及英语的动词词尾 -ise，共同撑起了这个拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the adjective practicus and the medieval verb practicare, both built on the idea of practical action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了形容词 practicus 与中世纪动词 practicare，两者都建立在「实际去做」这一念头上。

definition_zh: 赞美；表扬；赞颂；称赞的话
definition_en: to express strong approval or admiration for someone or something, or the words and worship that express it
core_image: 一群人把手举向台上，掌声像把某个人轻轻托高了一点
scene: 演出结束后全场站起来，掌声持续了很久，主唱却先转身向身后的年轻鼓手鞠了一躬。The crowd praised the drummer more than the singer they had come to see.
sceneCN: 这里 praise 是「称赞、表扬」（第 1 个义项：用言语表达赞许）；句意为观众对那位鼓手的称赞甚至超过他们专程来看的主唱。画面里有起立的观众、持续的掌声和转身鞠躬的主唱。

pos.zh: 赞美；表扬；颂扬
赞美；称赞的话；崇拜

derivatives.zh: praise 与 worthy 复合而成，义为「值得称赞的」
praise 加表示人的 -er 构成，义为「赞美者」
praise 加 -ful 构成，义为「充满赞美的」（较少使用）

senses.title: To express approval or admiration
senses.definition: to say that someone or something is good, or that you admire them
senses.definitionCN: 说某人或某物很好，或表达对他们的钦佩
senses.example: The teacher praised her for finishing the difficult task alone.
senses.exampleCN: 老师表扬她独自完成了那项困难的任务。
senses.why: The word began as a way of setting a value on something, so praise is literally saying how much someone is worth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是给某物定价的说法，所以 praise 字面上就是在说某个人值多少。

senses.title: Words that express approval
senses.definition: spoken or written words that show approval or admiration
senses.definitionCN: 口头上或书面上表达赞许与钦佩的话语
senses.example: Her first novel received high praise from several critics.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说得到了几位评论家的高度赞扬。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act of valuing, the same word can name the words that carry that valuation into public.
senses.whyCN: 动词既指「给出评价」这个动作，同一个词也就能指把这份评价带到人前的话语。

senses.title: To honour God in worship
senses.definition: to give honour and thanks to God, especially in a religious service
senses.definitionCN: 向上帝献上尊崇与感恩，尤指在宗教仪式中
senses.example: The congregation stood to praise God with a slow hymn.
senses.exampleCN: 会众起立，用一首缓慢的赞美诗颂扬上帝。
senses.why: Valuing something highly leads naturally to worship, so the word is used for the honour offered to a deity.
senses.whyCN: 把某样东西看得极高，自然会走向敬拜，于是这个词也用于向神灵献上的尊崇。

senses.title: Worship offered as an act
senses.definition: the honour and worship given to God, or a song or speech used for that purpose
senses.definitionCN: 献给上帝的尊崇与敬拜，或用于这一目的的诗歌与言辞
senses.example: The old book opens with a hymn of praise.
senses.exampleCN: 这本旧书以一首赞颂诗开篇。
senses.why: The noun keeps the religious branch alive beside the everyday one, especially in fixed phrases about worship.
senses.whyCN: 名词把宗教这一支与日常用法并存保留下来，尤其在关于敬拜的固定说法里。

intro.en: Praise comes from Latin words for price and value, passes through French, and still carries the idea of setting a worth on someone.
intro.cn: praise 来自拉丁语中表示价格与价值的词，经法语传入英语，至今仍带着「给某人估定价值」的意思。

items.en: Latin pretium meant price, value or worth, and it stands behind a whole family of words about judging what something is worth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pretium 意为价格、价值、分量，一整族表示「判断某物值多少」的词都从它而来。

items.en: Late Latin formed the verb pretiare, to value or to set a price on, which carried the idea into action.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语构成动词 pretiare，意为估价、给某物定价，把这个念头带进了动作。

items.en: Old French preisier meant to prize, to value and also to commend, and the sense of speaking well of someone grew out of the sense of valuing.
items.cn: 古法语 preisier 意为珍视、看重，也指称许；「说某人好话」这一层就是从「看重」长出来的。

items.en: Middle English preisen kept both the older sense of valuing and the newer sense of commending, and the spelling settled as praise.
items.cn: 中古英语 preisen 同时保留较早的「看重」与较新的「称许」，拼写后来定型为 praise。

items.en: Modern English keeps praise for spoken approval and for worship, while the old price sense survives in price, prize and appraise.
items.cn: 现代英语用 praise 表示口头赞许与敬拜，而古老的「价格」义则存活在 price、prize 与 appraise 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin family of valuing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs and nouns of approval and worship.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语中表示「估价」的词族；近义组收表示赞许与敬拜的动词和名词。

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something.
entries.definitionCN: 评估某物的价值或质量。

entries.definition: To recognize the value of something and be grateful for it.
entries.definitionCN: 认识到某物的价值并心怀感激。

entries.definition: The amount of money that something costs.
entries.definitionCN: 某物花费的金额；价格。

entries.definition: Something valuable given as a reward, or something held dear.
entries.definitionCN: 作为奖励的贵重之物，或被人珍视的东西。

entries.definition: To praise someone formally or officially.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或官方地称赞某人。

entries.definition: To clap in approval, or to praise a decision publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓掌表示赞许，或公开称赞某项决定。

entries.definition: A polite remark that expresses admiration.
entries.definitionCN: 表达钦佩的礼貌话语。

entries.definition: The honour and love given to a god or to someone greatly admired.
entries.definitionCN: 献给神灵或极受崇敬之人的尊崇与热爱。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin noun for price, a late verb for valuing and a French verb for prizing, with an English suffix for worth built on top.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把表示价格的拉丁名词、表示估价的晚期拉丁动词、表示珍视的法语动词合在一起，又在上面加了表示「值得」的英语后缀。

normal.en: Latin pretium is price, so to praise someone is to say that their worth is high.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pretium 是价格，所以 praise 一个人就是说他的价值很高。

normal.en: The same root gives price, prize and appraise, all of them about judging value.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 price、prize 与 appraise，全都与判断价值有关。

normal.en: Old French preisier meant both to value and to commend, and English kept both senses.
normal.cn: 古法语 preisier 既指看重也指称许，英语把两层都保留了下来。

normal.en: Praiseworthy joins praise and worthy, so it literally means worth praising.
normal.cn: praiseworthy 由 praise 与 worthy 拼合，字面就是「值得称赞的」。

normal.en: Praise is usually uncountable, but praises appears in phrases such as sing someone's praises.
normal.cn: praise 通常不可数，但 praises 会出现在 sing someone's praises 这类说法里。

abstract.en: Applause is value made audible: two hands striking together put a price on a performance.
abstract.cn: 掌声是价值发出了声音：两只手一拍，就等于给一场表演标了价。

abstract.en: Praise costs the speaker almost nothing and can still change what a person believes about themselves.
abstract.cn: 赞美几乎不花说话人什么成本，却仍能改变一个人对自己的看法。

abstract.en: A hymn of praise and a review of a novel use one word because both lift something above the ordinary.
abstract.cn: 赞美诗与小说评论用的是同一个词，因为两者都把某样东西托到平常之上。

examples.en: The crowd praised the drummer more than the singer.
examples.cn: 观众对鼓手的称赞甚至超过了主唱。

examples.en: Her first novel received high praise from several critics.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说得到了几位评论家的高度赞扬。

examples.en: The congregation stood to praise God with a slow hymn.
examples.cn: 会众起立，用一首缓慢的赞美诗颂扬上帝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来事」——好事扑到眼前，当然要夸一夸；记住 praise 是赞美。

root: 拉丁语 pretium（价格、价值）→ 晚期拉丁语 pretiare（估价、看重）→ 古法语 preisier（珍视、称许）→ 中古英语 preisen（看重、赞美）→ 现代英语 praise。同族的 price、prize、appraise、appreciate 都还带着「估定价值」的影子。

sensesIntro.en: The core is setting a high value on someone; it branches into spoken approval, the words themselves, and the honour given in worship.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是给某人估定很高的价值；由此分出当面的赞许、承载赞许的话语，以及献给神灵的崇敬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room of people lifting their hands in applause toward one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：满场的人抬手鼓掌，把掌声举向台上的一个人。

branches.en: a teacher nodding at a finished page
branches.cn: 老师对着写完的一页点头

branches.en: a review printed in a newspaper
branches.cn: 印在报纸上的一篇评论

branches.en: a slow hymn rising in a stone church
branches.cn: 石砌教堂里响起的一首缓慢赞美诗

branches.en: an old book opening with a song
branches.cn: 一本旧书以一首歌开篇

branches.en: hands clapping and words printed, saying the same thing
branches.cn: 鼓掌与见报的文字说着同一件事

intro.en: A Latin noun of price, a late verb of valuing and a French verb of prizing carry the word, with an English suffix for worth added on top.
intro.cn: 表示价格的拉丁名词、表示估价的晚期拉丁动词、表示珍视的法语动词撑起了这个词，上面又加了表示「值得」的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is well attested: pretium, pretiare and pretiosus all turn on the idea of value.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语这一层有明确记录：pretium、pretiare 与 pretiosus 都围绕「价值」这一念头。

definition_zh: 祈祷；祷告；恳求；央求；祈盼
definition_en: to speak to a god in worship or in request, and also to ask a person or fate for something with great earnestness
core_image: 一个人双手合在胸前，把心里的愿望说给看不见的听者
scene: 教堂里的灯很暗，老妇人在长椅前跪下，双手交握，嘴唇轻轻动着。She knelt in the dim church and began to pray for her grandson's recovery.
sceneCN: 这里是「祈祷、祷告」（第 1 个义项：向神说话）；句意为她在昏暗的教堂里跪下，开始为孙子的康复祈祷。图中可辨识物件：长椅、昏暗的灯、交握的双手。

pos.zh: 祈祷；祷告；恳求；祈盼

derivatives.zh: 由 pray 加 -er 构成的名词，指「祷告」或「祷文」；作「祈祷者」讲时读作 pray-er，与前者读音不同
prayer 加形容词后缀 -ful，义为「虔诚祈祷的」
prayerful 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「虔诚地祈祷着」

senses.title: To speak to a god in prayer
senses.definition: to address a god or a higher power, usually in words, in order to worship, give thanks or ask for help
senses.definitionCN: 向神或某种更高力量说话，通常用言语，以表达敬拜、感恩或求助
senses.example: The villagers pray in the small chapel every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们每天早晨都在小教堂里祈祷。
senses.why: The Latin verb precari meant to beg or entreat, so the oldest English use of pray is exactly this: turning a request toward someone believed to be able to answer it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 precari 本义是「恳求、央求」，pray 最早的意思正是如此：把请求说给一个被认为有能力回应的人听。

senses.title: To ask someone earnestly
senses.definition: to ask a person for something in a humble and urgent way, as though begging
senses.definitionCN: 以谦卑而急切的语气向某人提出请求，近乎哀求
senses.example: I pray you, do not tell him what I said.
senses.exampleCN: 我求您了，别把我说的告诉他。
senses.why: Because the word began as an act of begging, it could be aimed at a person as easily as at a god; this everyday sense still survives in set phrases such as pray tell.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就表示「乞求」，所以既可以对着神说，也可以对着人说；这一日常义项仍保留在 pray tell 这类固定说法里。

senses.title: To hope for something very strongly
senses.definition: to want something to happen very much, often expressed as a wish rather than a request to any particular listener
senses.definitionCN: 非常希望某事发生，往往只是表达愿望，并不真的说给某个特定听者
senses.example: We pray that the rains come before the wells run dry.
senses.exampleCN: 我们祈盼在井水干涸之前下雨。
senses.why: Once praying is framed as a request for an outcome, the outcome itself can fill the whole meaning, so the verb slides from talking to a god into simply hoping hard.
senses.whyCN: 当祈祷被理解成「为某个结果提出请求」，结果本身就占满了整个词义，于是动词从「对神说话」滑向「强烈地盼望」。

senses.title: Please, in old-fashioned polite formulas
senses.definition: used in older or formal English to soften a request, roughly meaning please
senses.definitionCN: 在较古旧或正式的英语中用来缓和请求，大致相当于「请」
senses.example: Pray be seated; the doctor will see you shortly.
senses.exampleCN: 请坐，医生很快就给您看诊。
senses.why: The begging sense weakened into pure politeness, so the verb became a formula for softening a request, much as please did.
senses.whyCN: 「乞求」的语气逐渐弱化成纯粹的礼貌，动词便成了缓和请求的套语，作用和 please 相近。

intro.en: Pray comes from a Latin verb of begging; the religious sense is a specialised use of that older, everyday act of asking.
intro.cn: pray 来自拉丁语中表示「乞求」的动词；宗教上的「祈祷」只是这个更古老、更日常的「求人」动作的专门用法。

items.en: A root usually reconstructed as *prek-, meaning to ask or request, is thought to lie behind the Latin verb; the form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁动词背后有一个常被重构为 *prek- 的词根，意为「请求、询问」；这是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Precari meant to entreat, beg or ask, and its noun prex, with the stem prec-, named a prayer or a request.
items.cn: precari 意为恳求、乞求、请求，其名词 prex（词干 prec-）指祈祷或请求。

items.en: Old French preier, later written prier, meant both to ask a person and to address God, and it is the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 preier（后来写作 prier）既指向人请求，也指向神说话，英语借的正是这个形式。

items.en: Middle English prayen carried the double sense of asking a person and praying to God, and the spelling settled as pray.
items.cn: 中古英语 prayen 同时保留「求人」和「求神」两义，拼写后来固定为 pray。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious sense as the main one; the older begging sense survives in fixed phrases, and the derived noun prayer has developed a shortened pronunciation of its own.
items.cn: 现代英语以宗教义为主；较古的「恳求」义残留在固定短语中，派生名词 prayer 也发展出自己缩短的读音。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share letters or the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of asking or of addressing a higher power.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近或同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收其他表示「请求」或「向更高力量说话」的词。

entries.definition: An animal hunted by another animal for food; from Latin praeda.
entries.definitionCN: 猎物；被捕食的动物。只是读音与拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The noun built on pray, naming the act or the words of praying.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pray 派生的名词，指祈祷的行为或祷文。

entries.definition: To look too closely into something private, or to force something open.
entries.definitionCN: 窥探；撬开。只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To express disapproval of something; from Latin deprecari, literally to pray away.
entries.definitionCN: 反对；不赞成。源自拉丁语 deprecari，字面是「祈祷着把某事推开」。

entries.definition: To ask for something in an urgent or humble way.
entries.definitionCN: 急切或卑微地请求；乞求。

entries.definition: To ask for something in a serious and emotional way.
entries.definitionCN: 恳切地请求；恳求。

entries.definition: To ask someone urgently and sincerely for something.
entries.definitionCN: 恳切而真诚地请求；哀求。

entries.definition: To show deep respect and love for a god, especially in a service.
entries.definitionCN: 敬拜；礼拜，尤指在仪式中表达对神的敬爱与尊崇。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of begging, and its family shows how asking a person turned into addressing a god.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「乞求」的动词，它的同族词显示出「求人」如何转成「求神」。

normal.en: Precari in Latin means to beg; pray keeps that posture of asking rather than demanding.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 precari 意为乞求，pray 保留了「请求」而不是「要求」的姿态。

normal.en: Prec- is the stem of prex, a prayer or request, so the same stem carries the act of asking.
normal.cn: prec- 是 prex（祈祷、请求）的词干，同一个词干承载着「请求」这个动作。

normal.en: Pray for peace, pray for rain: the pattern pray for plus a thing names what you want to happen.
normal.cn: pray for peace、pray for rain：pray for 后面接一件事，就点明了希望发生什么。

normal.en: Pray tell is a fossil of the old sense: there pray means I beg you, not I worship.
normal.cn: pray tell 是旧义的化石：那里的 pray 意为「我求您」，而不是「我敬拜」。

normal.en: A praying mantis is named for its raised forelegs, which look like hands held in prayer.
normal.cn: praying mantis（螳螂）得名于它举起的前足，看上去像合十祈祷的手。

abstract.en: Praying is a wish given an address: the same words would be only a hope if no one were listening.
abstract.cn: 祈祷是给愿望写上了收件人：若没有听者，同样的话就只是希望。

abstract.en: Asking a person and asking a god use the same verb, which quietly admits how alike the two acts feel.
abstract.cn: 求人和求神用同一个动词，这等于默认两种动作在感觉上多么相似。

abstract.en: A prayer may leave the world unchanged, but it usually leaves the speaker rearranged.
abstract.cn: 祈祷未必改变世界，却往往把祈祷的人重新整理了一遍。

examples.en: She knelt by the bed and prayed for her son.
examples.cn: 她在床边跪下，为儿子祈祷。

examples.en: We pray that the bridge holds until help arrives.
examples.cn: 我们祈盼这座桥能撑到救援到来。

examples.en: Pray tell me what happened at the meeting.
examples.cn: 请告诉我会上发生了什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑雷」——急得心里扑通打雷，只好开口求人；pray 便是恳求、祈祷。

root: 拉丁语 precari（恳求、祈求），名词 prex（词干 prec-，祈祷、请求）；经古法语 preier 进入英语，同族词多与「请求」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a request sent upward; the senses divide by who is addressed, a god, a person, or no one in particular, and by how far the request has faded into politeness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「向上发出的请求」；义项按说给谁听分出向神、向人、只对结果说话三等，也按请求语气的弱化分出客套用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with hands pressed together, sending a wish toward a listener who cannot be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人双手合十，把愿望送给一个看不见的听者。

branches.en: a woman kneeling in a dim chapel, whispering a request
branches.cn: 昏暗小教堂里跪着低声祈求的女人

branches.en: a servant on one knee, begging his master for mercy
branches.cn: 单膝跪地、向主人求饶的仆人

branches.en: a farmer watching the sky, asking for rain that may not come
branches.cn: 农夫望着天，求一场也许不会来的雨

branches.en: a letter ending with one courtly please
branches.cn: 一封信末尾那句客气的「请」

branches.en: the same raised hands, once to a god and once to the weather
branches.cn: 同样举起的双手，一次朝着神，一次朝着天气

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of entreaty, its noun stem, an Old French reshaping, and English endings that mark the person and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示恳求的动词、它的名词词干、古法语的改写，以及标记「人」与「性质」的英语词尾共同构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb of entreaty and its noun stem, which English later reshaped through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示恳求的动词及其名词词干，英语又经法语对它做了改写。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 祈祷着把某事推开；祈求免除

senses.title: The act of speaking to a god
senses.definition: the act of speaking to a god, silently or aloud, in order to worship, give thanks or ask for something
senses.definitionCN: 向神说话的行为，可以默念也可以出声，用以敬拜、感恩或求助
senses.example: Her morning prayer takes about ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她早晨的祷告大约要十分钟。
senses.why: The noun is the verb pray with a French-shaped ending, so its first job is simply to give the activity a name.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是在动词 pray 后面接上一个法语式的词尾构成的，所以它最基本的作用就是把动词所描述的活动变成一个名字。

senses.title: The words used in praying
senses.definition: a fixed or composed set of words spoken or read when praying
senses.definitionCN: 祈祷时说出或读出的固定文本，或临时组织的一段话
senses.example: The children learned the Lord's Prayer by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把《主祷文》背了下来。
senses.why: Once the activity has a name, the words that carry it can be named too, so a prayer becomes a text that can be learned, printed and repeated.
senses.whyCN: 活动有了名字之后，承载这场活动的那些话也就可以被命名，于是 prayer 成为可以背诵、印刷、反复念的文本。

senses.title: A person who prays
senses.definition: someone who prays, formed as pray plus -er and pronounced with two syllables
senses.definitionCN: 做祈祷的人，由 pray 加 -er 构成，读作两个音节
senses.example: A faithful prayer, she attends the dawn service every day.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个虔诚的祈祷者，每天都参加清晨的礼拜。
senses.why: English often adds -er to a verb to name the doer, so pray plus -er gives a person; that spelling is said pray-er, while the noun for the act has lost its second syllable.
senses.whyCN: 英语常给动词加 -er 来表示「做这件事的人」，pray 加 -er 便指祈祷的人；这个写法读作 pray-er，而表示行为的名词已经把第二个音节省掉了。

senses.title: An earnest hope or request
senses.definition: something strongly hoped for, often spoken of as if it were a request made to fate
senses.definitionCN: 殷切盼望的事，常被说成仿佛是对命运提出的请求
senses.example: It is my prayer that the two sides will talk again.
senses.exampleCN: 我祈盼双方能够再次坐下来谈。
senses.why: If a prayer is a request, then the thing requested can take the same name, which is why the word can mean the wish itself rather than the words or the act.
senses.whyCN: 既然祷告是一种请求，被请求的那件事也可以沿用同一个词，于是 prayer 能指愿望本身，而不只是话语或行为。

intro.en: The noun grew out of the Latin verb of entreaty, took its shape in French, and split in pronunciation from the person who prays.
intro.cn: 这个名词从拉丁语中表示恳求的动词长出来，在法语里定型，后来读音又与「祈祷的人」分了家。

items.en: The verb precari meant to entreat or beg, and it stands behind both the verb pray and the noun prayer.
items.cn: 动词 precari 意为恳求、乞求，pray 与 prayer 两个词都源于它。

items.en: A noun use of the same stem, precaria meant entreaty or the things one begs for, and it supplied the shape of the later noun.
items.cn: 同一词干的名词用法 precaria 指恳求或所乞求之物，为后来的名词提供了形态基础。

items.en: Old French preiere meant a prayer or an entreaty and was the form English borrowed for the noun.
items.cn: 古法语 preiere 意为祈祷、恳求，英语借的正是这个名词形式。

items.en: Middle English used prayer for both the act and the words, and the spelling settled without the final -e of the French form.
items.cn: 中古英语用 prayer 兼指祈祷的行为和祷词，拼写定型时去掉了法语词尾的 -e。

items.en: Modern English says the noun for the act as /preə/, while the person who prays keeps a fuller pray-er sound; the two uses drifted apart in speech.
items.cn: 现代英语把指行为的名词读作 /preə/，而「祈祷的人」保留了更完整的 pray-er 读音；两种用法在口语里逐渐分开。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the verb and the family built around it; the near-meaning group gathers words for devotion and for urgent asking.
note.cn: 形近组收动词本身及其词族；近义组收表示虔诚、敬拜或急切请求的词。

entries.definition: The verb that prayer is built on, meaning to speak to a god or to beg.
entries.definitionCN: prayer 所由构成的动词，意为祈祷或恳求。

entries.definition: Given to prayer; showing devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 常做祷告的；虔诚的。

entries.definition: An animal hunted for food by another animal.
entries.definitionCN: 猎物；被捕食的动物。只是读音相同、拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Too eager to know about other people's private affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 爱打听别人私事的。只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Deep love and loyalty shown to a god or to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 对神或对人的深切爱戴与忠诚；虔诚。

entries.definition: A humble and urgent request made to someone in power.
entries.definitionCN: 向掌权者低声而急切地提出的请求；恳求。

entries.definition: The activity of showing reverence to a god, often in a service.
entries.definitionCN: 对神的敬拜，常在仪式中进行。

entries.definition: An emotional request made when someone is in trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 身处困境时提出的恳切请求。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the verb plus an ending, and the endings it carries keep pointing back to the act of praying.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词就是动词加一个词尾，而它携带的词尾始终指向「祈祷」这个动作。

normal.en: The noun is the verb plus an ending, so anything the verb can do, the noun can name as an activity.
normal.cn: 这个名词就是动词加一个词尾，因此动词能做的事，名词都能把它当作一种活动来命名。

normal.en: The second syllable vanished: what was pray-er for the act became prayer, while the person kept a clearer pray-er sound.
normal.cn: 第二个音节消失了：指行为的 pray-er 变成 prayer，而指人的说法则保留了更清楚的 pray-er 读音。

normal.en: Say a prayer: the verb say shows that a prayer can be a piece of language, not only a feeling.
normal.cn: say a prayer 这个搭配里的 say 说明 prayer 可以是一段话语，而不只是一种心情。

normal.en: The Lord's Prayer is a fixed text, a clear example of prayer as words rather than as an act.
normal.cn: 《主祷文》是一段固定文本，清楚展示了 prayer 作为「话语」而非「行为」的用法。

normal.en: Prayer book and prayer meeting keep the noun in compounds, where the first element names the purpose.
normal.cn: prayer book 和 prayer meeting 把这个名词留在复合词里，前一部分说明用途。

abstract.en: A prayer is the shape a wish takes when it is spoken to someone who may not answer.
abstract.cn: 祷告是一个愿望在被说给未必回应的人听时所采取的形态。

abstract.en: The same letters cover an act, a text and a person, and only the voice tells them apart.
abstract.cn: 同样几个字母同时指行为、文本和人，只有读音把它们区分开。

abstract.en: People rarely pray calmly; the word is loudest when nothing else can be done.
abstract.cn: 人很少心平气和地祷告；当别的办法都没有时，这个词最响。

examples.en: Saying a prayer before meals is a habit in her family.
examples.cn: 饭前祷告是她家的习惯。

examples.en: The letter read like a prayer for forgiveness.
examples.cn: 那封信读起来像一篇祈求宽恕的祷文。

examples.en: His prayer was that the ship would reach the shore.
examples.cn: 他祈盼船能靠岸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞尔」——声音软下来，像是把话轻轻说给天上听；prayer 就是祷告。

root: 拉丁语 precari（恳求）的名词形式 precaria 经古法语 preiere 进入英语；与动词 pray 同源，但读音走了两条路。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of praying; from it come the words used, the person who prays, and the wish that is prayed for.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「祈祷」这一行为；由它分出所用的祷词、做祈祷的人，以及被祈求的那个愿望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands joined above a page of fixed words, repeated until they are known by heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：合十的双手悬在一页固定文字之上，反复念到能背下来。

branches.en: a woman closing her eyes at the side of a hospital corridor
branches.cn: 医院走廊边闭眼的女人

branches.en: a child reciting a text learned by heart
branches.cn: 背诵一段熟记文字的孩子

branches.en: an old worshipper kneeling longer than the others
branches.cn: 跪得比别人久的老人

branches.en: a sentence written at the end of a letter, asking fate for a favour
branches.cn: 信末写下的那句话，向命运讨一个人情

branches.en: the same words passed from one pair of hands to the next
branches.cn: 同样的话语从一双手传到另一双手

intro.en: The noun is the Latin verb of entreaty reshaped by a Latin noun ending and then by French, with English suffixes growing from the result.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁语中表示恳求的动词，经拉丁名词词尾和法语先后改写而成，再由英语后缀长出新的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both the verb of entreaty and the noun built on it; French then trimmed the word into the shape English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语既提供了表示恳求的动词，也提供了由它构成的名词；法语随后把它修剪成英语借用的形状。

items.meaning: forms nouns of state or result
items.meaningCN: 构成表示状态或结果的名词

items.meaning: the act or words of praying

definition_zh: 预防措施；防备；防范；安全防护安排
definition_en: something done in advance to stop trouble from happening, and the care taken before a risk arrives
core_image: 出门前那双手把门窗与煤气阀逐一检查一遍
scene: 台风消息传来，店主把窗板一块块钉上，又把沙袋堆在门缝前。As a precaution, the shopkeeper boarded up the windows before the storm arrived.
sceneCN: 这里是「预防措施、防备」（第 1 个义项：事先采取的防范做法）；句意为台风到来前，店主把窗户钉上作为防备。图中可辨识物件：窗板、沙袋、店门。

pos.zh: 预防措施；防备；防范；安全防护安排

derivatives.zh: 由 precaution 加形容词后缀 -ary 构成，义为「预防性的；防备的」
precautionary 加 -ly 构成，义为「以预防的方式」

senses.title: A step taken in advance to prevent harm
senses.definition: an action done before a risk arrives, so that the harm it could cause is avoided or reduced
senses.definitionCN: 在风险到来之前就做好的动作，用来避免或减轻它可能造成的伤害
senses.example: Take precautions against theft when you travel.
senses.exampleCN: 出门旅行时要采取防盗措施。
senses.why: The word names a guarding that happens before the danger, so the most common sense is the concrete thing a person does ahead of time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指的是在危险之前完成的「看守」，所以最常见的义项就是人提前做的那件具体的事。

senses.title: Care taken beforehand
senses.definition: the habit or act of being careful in advance, rather than one single measure
senses.definitionCN: 提前保持小心的习惯或做法，而不是某一项具体措施
senses.example: He moved the papers with great precaution, as if they might tear.
senses.exampleCN: 他非常小心地搬动那些文件，仿佛它们随时会破。
senses.why: Strip away the countable measure and what remains is the quality behind it: a watchfulness that starts before anything has gone wrong.
senses.whyCN: 把可数的具体措施抽掉，剩下的是它背后的性质：在事情出错之前就已经开始的警觉。

senses.title: Official safety arrangements
senses.definition: the set of rules and arrangements an institution keeps in place for one particular kind of danger
senses.definitionCN: 机构为某一类危险而长期设置的一整套规定与安排
senses.example: The hotel's fire precautions were inspected last month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆的消防安排上个月接受了检查。
senses.why: Because measures against one kind of danger are planned together, the plural came to name an organised set rather than separate acts.
senses.whyCN: 针对同一类危险的措施通常是配套规划的，于是复数形式便用来指一套有组织的安排，而不是零散的动作。

intro.en: Precaution is a Latin compound meaning a guarding done before the event, which French passed on to English.
intro.cn: precaution 是一个拉丁语复合词，意为「在事情之前完成的看守」，经法语传入英语。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, in place as well as in time, so it adds the idea of doing something ahead of the event.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前」，既指空间上的前面，也指时间上的先前，因此给词根加上「提前」的意思。

items.en: Cavere meant to be on guard, to take care or to watch out, and it also gave English caution and caveat.
items.cn: cavere 意为当心、提防、留意，英语的 caution 与 caveat 也来自它。

items.en: Joined together, prae- and cavere produced praecautio, a guarding done beforehand, with the noun ending -tio naming the action.
items.cn: prae- 与 cavere 合起来构成 praecautio，指「事先做的提防」，名词词尾 -tio 表示动作。

items.en: French took the Latin noun as précaution and passed it into English, where the accent was soon dropped from the spelling.
items.cn: 法语把这一拉丁名词写作 précaution 并传入英语，英语拼写随后去掉了重音符号。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for both the prior care and the concrete measures that carry it out, with the plural naming a set of safety arrangements.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它指事先的谨慎，也指落实这种谨慎的具体措施；复数则指一整套安全安排。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the two Latin parts and the caution family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for protection taken in advance.
note.cn: 形近组沿两个拉丁构件与 caution 词族展开；近义组收其他表示「提前防护」的词。

entries.definition: Care taken to avoid danger; from the same Latin verb cavere.
entries.definitionCN: 避免危险的谨慎；与 precaution 同出拉丁动词 cavere。

entries.definition: Careful to avoid risk or danger.
entries.definitionCN: 小心避开风险或危险的；谨慎的。

entries.definition: A warning that something may not be true or may fail.
entries.definitionCN: 提醒某事可能不成立或会出问题的警告。

entries.definition: Acting as a protection against something that might happen.
entries.definitionCN: 起预防作用的；防备性的。

entries.definition: Something that protects people from harm or loss.
entries.definitionCN: 保护人们免受伤害或损失的东西；保障措施。

entries.definition: An action taken to deal with a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 为处理某个问题而采取的行动；措施。

entries.definition: The state of being kept safe from harm.
entries.definitionCN: 受到保护、免于伤害的状态。

entries.definition: Careful thinking about what will be needed later.
entries.definitionCN: 对日后需要的东西所做的预先考虑。

normalIntro.en: Two Latin parts, a prefix of before and a verb of watching, combine into one noun that always looks ahead.
normalIntro.cn: 两个拉丁构件，一个表示「在前」的前缀和一个表示「看守」的动词，合成一个总是朝前看的名字。

normal.en: Praecautio is literally a guarding before: prae- adds before, cavere adds the watching.
normal.cn: praecautio 字面就是「事先的看守」：prae- 加上「在前」，cavere 加上「看守」。

normal.en: Caution is the heart of the word and cautious is its adjective, so the family always points to care rather than to repair.
normal.cn: caution 是这个词的核心，cautious 是它的形容词，可见这个词族总是指向「小心」，而不是「事后修补」。

normal.en: Take precautions: the verb take shows that these are things you carry out, not feelings you have.
normal.cn: take precautions 里的 take 说明这些是可以执行的做法，而不是心里的感觉。

normal.en: As a precaution works like an adverbial phrase, naming the reason for an action rather than the action itself.
normal.cn: as a precaution 起状语短语的作用，说明做某事的理由，而不是那件事本身。

normal.en: Caveat comes from the same Latin verb and means let him beware, a warning rather than a measure.
normal.cn: caveat 出自同一个拉丁动词，意思是「让他当心」，是警告而不是措施。

abstract.en: A precaution is a bet paid in advance against a loss you hope never arrives.
abstract.cn: 预防措施是为一场你希望永不发生的损失提前付下的赌注。

abstract.en: The word puts care before the event, which is why it never describes a rescue.
abstract.cn: 这个词把「小心」放在事件之前，所以它从不描述救援。

abstract.en: Every precaution admits that something can go wrong, and does something about it anyway.
abstract.cn: 每一个预防措施都承认事情可能出错，却仍然为此做了点什么。

examples.en: Take precautions against fire before the dry season begins.
examples.cn: 旱季到来之前要采取防火措施。

examples.en: She copied the files as a precaution.
examples.cn: 她把文件复制了一份，以防万一。

examples.en: The factory's safety precautions were found to be inadequate.
examples.cn: 这家工厂的安全防范措施被认定不到位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑瑞考神」——出门前先扑上去求考神保佑，就是预防；precaution 是预防措施。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前、预先）+ cavere（当心、提防）→ praecautio（事先的提防）→ 法语 précaution → 英语 precaution。

sensesIntro.en: The core is care placed before the event; the senses divide into the prior watchfulness, the single step that carries it out, and the organised set of such steps.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「放在事情之前的谨慎」；义项分出事先的警觉、落实警觉的单项做法，以及成套的这类做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of hands checking the door and the gas valve before leaving the house.
core.cn: 核心意象：出门前那双手把门窗和煤气阀逐一检查一遍。

branches.en: boards nailed over a shop window before a storm
branches.cn: 台风前钉在店窗上的木板

branches.en: a hand pausing to test whether the stove is off
branches.cn: 一只手停下来试炉子是否关好

branches.en: a printed list of fire rules on a factory wall
branches.cn: 工厂墙上印着的一列消防规定

branches.en: sandbags at the door and a checklist on the wall
branches.cn: 门口的沙袋与墙上的检查清单

branches.en: the quiet habit of looking twice before locking up
branches.cn: 锁门前习惯性多看一遍的安静举动

intro.en: Two Latin parts, a prefix of before and a verb of watching, combine into one noun; English then added a suffix for the adjective.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁构件，表示「在前」的前缀和表示「看守」的动词，合成一个名词；英语再为它加上构成形容词的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the prefix and the verb, and the compound noun built from them; French carried that noun into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了前缀、动词以及由二者构成的复合名词；法语把这个名词带进了英语。
